documents.name: Job Description for Automation Specialist.pdf
documents.content: 04/12/2024, 21:01 Job Description for Automation Specialist Job Description for Automation Specialist About Impact Operations: Impact Operations is a fast-growing, purpose-driven company specializing in building and optimizing systems that empower businesses to scale effectively. Our mission is to create systems that drive data-focused decisions and efficiency for our clients, who are purpose-driven coaches. Position Overview: We are seeking a dedicated Automation Specialist to join our team. This role offers an exciting opportunity for a detail-oriented individual with a passion for workflow automation and data reporting. As an Automation Specialist, you will play a crucial role in streamlining processes, optimizing data workflows, and contributing to the overall efficiency of our operations. Key Responsibilities: • Workflow Automation: Utilize Make and Zapier to automate tasks, workflows, and data integrations across different platforms, ensuring smooth and efficient operations within the organization. • Cross-functional Collaboration: Work closely with different teams to identify automation opportunities, understand requirements, and implement effective solutions that align with business needs. • Monitoring and Troubleshooting: Regularly monitor automated processes, quickly address any issues or errors, and troubleshoot to ensure smooth and consistent operation. • Data Reporting: Develop and maintain data solutions using Looker Studio to connect and extract data from various sources, including Google Sheets, MySQL, Facebook Ads Manager, and Google Analytics. • Documentation and Knowledge Sharing: Create and maintain clear documentation for automated processes, facilitating knowledge transfer and ensuring transparency within the team. https://impactops.notion.site/Job-Description-for-Automation-Specialist-2cc57982de394e7d8378f2821c1474dd 1/3 04/12/2024, 21:01 Job Description for Automation Specialist • Continuous Learning: Stay updated on the latest trends, tools, and best practices related to automation and data analytics to continually enhance existing processes. Qualifications: • Technical Proficiency: Experience with automation tools like Looker Studio, Make, and Zapier, with a strong ability to connect and integrate data from various sources. • Problem-Solving Skills: Ability to identify issues in automated workflows, troubleshoot effectively, and develop solutions to complex automation challenges. • Attention to Detail: A commitment to maintaining accuracy in data reporting and ensuring precise execution of automated workflows. • Collaboration Skills: Strong communication skills to work effectively within cross-functional teams, ensuring alignment and successful implementation of automation solutions. • Adaptability: Willingness to learn new technologies, stay updated with industry trends, and continuously improve automation capabilities. Compensation & Benefits: • Hourly Rate: $10/hr - $15/hr, depending on experience. • Growth Opportunity: Potential for skill development and advancement within the company based on performance. • Supportive Environment: A collaborative team dedicated to helping you succeed and grow in your role. • Training: Comprehensive onboarding and continuous learning opportunities to keep your skills sharp. Why Join Us? • Purpose-Driven Work: Be part of a company that values your contributions and is committed to making a positive impact on our clients and team members. • Innovation and Efficiency: Work in an environment that encourages innovation and supports the implementation of new ideas to improve our systems and processes. https://impactops.notion.site/Job-Description-for-Automation-Specialist-2cc57982de394e7d8378f2821c1474dd 2/3 04/12/2024, 21:01 Job Description for Automation Specialist • Flexibility: Enjoy the benefits of remote work with a supportive and collaborative team. Application Process: To apply, please submit your resume and a brief cover letter explaining your interest in the Automation Specialist role at Impact Operations. Be sure to include specific examples of your experience with workflow automation and data reporting tools. https://impactops.notion.site/Job-Description-for-Automation-Specialist-2cc57982de394e7d8378f2821c1474dd 3/3

documents.name: Creating a new Onboarding Challenge - SOP.pdf
documents.content: 04/12/2024, 21:02 Creating a new Onboarding Challenge - SOP Creating a new Onboarding Challenge - SOP What is an Onboarding Challenge? • An onboarding challenge is a 1-2 week project that we assign to a new hire to test their skills and see if they are capable of completing a project or series of projects that emulate a real situation they will be in when theyʼre brought in as a full time team member. Philosophy of Onboarding Challenges • The philosophy of an onboarding challenge is to give new hires a chance to put their skills to the test and for the hiring manager to assess the skills of the new hire. It gives both parties an opportunity to test the waters before the working relationship begins. • This allows the new team member to have an opportunity to get an understanding of what their role will be like in the safety of a staging environment without risking any client assets https://impactops.notion.site/Creating-a-new-Onboarding-Challenge-SOP-6da676cf402e436e874d29fa9131f70b 1/3 04/12/2024, 21:02 Creating a new Onboarding Challenge - SOP • This allows the hiring manager an opportunity to see the quality of the work that the new hire is able to produce and gives a clearer picture on what the working relationship will be like with that tentative new employee. This is better than reviewing a portfolio because we can assess many aspects of the development process such as: ◦ How long it takes people to complete different tasks ◦ How developed their problem solving abilities are ◦ How many questions they ask vs. how autonomous they are ◦ The type of questions they ask are an indication of how reliant they are on instruction and oversight ▪ If they ask “How” questions like “How do I do {blank}?” then you know they may be more dependent on direction and oversight and are less autonomous in ideating solutions for themselves. ▪ If they ask “What” questions like “What is the added criteria of this particular aspect of the onboarding challenge?” then that shows they are thinking critically about the situation presented in the challenge and are asking for further clarity to be able to develop a solution • We do not give away ALL information within the Onboarding Challenge. We want to intentionally exclude certain information from the prompt (specifically “How” portions of the prompt) to assess their problem solving abilities. https://impactops.notion.site/Creating-a-new-Onboarding-Challenge-SOP-6da676cf402e436e874d29fa9131f70b 2/3 04/12/2024, 21:02 Creating a new Onboarding Challenge - SOP • Example of how we could exclude “How” details: ◦ We would outline in the description of the challenge something like this: “Once this link is clicked, if they do not opt-in for xyz after x period of time, send an email to the contact to prompt them to opt-in. If they do opt-in, send an email that confirms their opt-in” ◦ There are multiple easter eggs hidden in this one piece of instruction: ▪ This piece of instruction is basically telling them to set up a 3 different workflows: • 1 announcement workflow that promptʼs them to opt-in. When they click on the trigger link in the original message, they will get added to another workflow (Abandoned Cart Sequence). If they do not opt-in, they will not receive a tag after x period of time and we would want to check whether or not the tag exists before sending the first email mentioned in the instruction • If they do go on to opt-in, they would need to ensure a tag would be added to the contact to show that they opted in. This tag would trigger the confirmation workflow. This confirmation sequence would need to ensure the contact is removed from both of the previous workflows to ensure multiple pieces of incorrect communication do not go out. Then after all of this happens, they would receive the confirmation email ◦ Using this 1 example you can see how much deduction, strategic thinking and skill would be required to be able to develop this solution as explained above. The intention is NOT that the person would be able to anticipate the need to account for ALL of the aforementioned features (unless they havepreviousexperiencesolvingforthisexacttypeofusecase) https://impactops.notion.site/Creating-a-new-Onboarding-Challenge-SOP-6da676cf402e436e874d29fa9131f70b 3/3

documents.name: Business Operations Course Sub-Bullets Draft.docx
documents.content: Business Operations Course Purpose: turn business operations into a repeatable, teachable framework Format: live sessions recorded, turned into Trainual modules Org Chart Define current structure (departments and reporting lines) Design the ideal future-state structure for scalability Clarify leadership responsibilities and decision-making authority Keep updated as the company evolves Company Goal Define one clear, measurable annual objective (north star) Break down into quarterly milestones Align all divisions and KPIs to this goal Communicate and check in goals progress weekly with the entire team Division Goals Translate company goal into specific division-level targets Assign ownership to division leads Ensure goals are measurable and ensure timings for each Review alignment with company-wide scoreboard Adjust quarterly based on business needs Scoreboards Company-level scoreboard (tracks progress toward the annual goal) Division scoreboards (tracks team-specific KPIs) Action scoreboard (tracks tactical tasks and deliverables) Visual, easy-to-understand format (numbers, charts, green/red status) Reviewed weekly by leadership and teams Action Scoreboard Focus on leading indicators (daily/weekly actions) Tied directly to division and company goals Assign ownership for each action item Reviewed during weekly meetings Helps identify bottlenecks early Benchmarking Current State and Future State Document the current process, structure, and results Define what “future state” looks like (ideal metrics, workflows) Compare gaps between current and future state Prioritize improvement opportunities Create a timeline to move from current to future Process Flow Maps Visual representation of each core business process Show inputs, outputs, and handoffs between teams Identify inefficiencies and bottlenecks Standardize steps to reduce variability Update regularly as processes improve SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures) Write clear, step-by-step instructions for each recurring process Assign ownership for maintaining/updating SOPs Store in a centralized system (e.g., Trainual) Include screenshots, templates, and examples for clarity Review/update every quarter of the year Continuous Improvement Build a culture of ongoing process optimization Encourage employees to suggest improvements Review performance data regularly for trends Run small experiments to test new ideas Document changes and lessons learned New Process Rollout Communicate clearly why the process is changing Provide training and support materials (SOPs, videos, checklists) Assign process champions to support adoption Pilot with a small group before full rollout Monitor adoption and gather feedback Quality Control on New Processes Define key success metrics for each new process Audit compliance during the first 30 days Collect feedback Iterate/Adjust the process based on findings Approve as “final” only after consistent results Trainual Central hub for all company knowledge and SOPs Organize content by department and topic Use multimedia (text, screenshots, videos) for training Assign required trainings to new hires and existing staff Track completion and quiz scores Turn Business into a University Build structured training paths for each role Combine technical skills + culture/values training Use quizzes, certifications, and progress tracking Update regularly to stay relevant Promote continuous learning as part of company culture Identify the Perfect Person and Build Training Define role expectations and required skills List “ideal behaviors” aligned with company values Create a 30/60/90 training roadmap for new hires Build advanced training for high performers Use data to measure training effectiveness Core Pillars of Business Sales & Marketing (revenue generation) Operations (delivery & efficiency) Finance (profitability & sustainability) HR (recruiting, culture, leadership development) Sunday Business Planning Weekly leadership meeting to set priorities Review scoreboards and KPIs Align on key projects for the week Assign owners to action items Ensure all divisions are aligned with company goals Project Kickoff Define project scope, timeline, and success criteria Assign project lead and team members Set up project tools (ClickUp, Slack channels, etc.) Communicate kickoff plan to all stakeholders Document initial plan in a shared environment Project Updates Weekly check-ins with project team Update ClickUp tasks and dashboards Flag blockers early to leadership Share progress updates in team meetings Adjust timeline/resources if needed Action Items List Centralized list of all assigned tasks Each item has a clear owner and due date Regularly reviewed in meetings Mark off once completed Prevents “lost tasks” across teams Escalation to Leadership Define what issues should be escalated (budget, delays, client risks) Create a clear escalation pathway Use structured format (problem, impact, proposed solution) Leadership provides decision or direction quickly Document outcomes for accountability Disciplining Using Core Values Core values as the framework for feedback Address issues directly Give employees a chance to improve (coaching plan) Escalate to formal write-up if repeated Ensure fairness and alignment with culture Reporting Updates to Leadership Weekly reports on division performance Highlight wins, challenges, and KPIs Use dashboards for quick visibility Provide recommended actions, not just data Keep updates concise and actionable Finance Management Accurate bookkeeping and reconciliations Cash flow tracking (in/out timing) Regular budget reviews Align spending with strategic goals Use reports to guide decision-making P&L (Profit & Loss) Review revenue, COGS, and expenses monthly Track gross margin and net profit Compare to budget and prior periods Identify cost overruns or revenue shortfalls Share insights with leadership team Accrual vs. Cash Basis Understand differences in accounting methods Accrual = revenue/expenses recorded when earned/incurred Cash = revenue/expenses recorded when money changes hands Decide which method best suits business needs Ensure consistency in reporting Expense Reduction – Getting Lean Review all expenses quarterly Cut unnecessary or low-ROI spending Negotiate better vendor terms Automate manual processes to save time/money Reinvest savings into growth areas Creating a Budget Forecast revenue and expenses annually Allocate resources by department Include buffer for unexpected costs Get leadership approval before finalizing Review monthly to stay on track Budget vs. Actuals Compare budgeted vs. actual performance monthly Highlight variances (positive or negative) Investigate causes of variance Adjust future budgets based on learnings Share insights with department heads Recruiting Define the role and ideal candidate profile Write clear, compelling job descriptions Post jobs across multiple platforms Standardize interview process Track candidates in an ATS The Culture Index Use assessments to evaluate personality/fit Compare candidate profiles to role requirements Understand team dynamics through data Use insights for coaching and leadership development Align hiring with company culture Job Creation Identify need for a new role (workload, skill gap, growth) Define responsibilities and KPIs Ensure alignment with company goals Get leadership approval before posting Add role into org chart Applicant Tracking System (ATS) Centralize candidate applications Track progress through stages (applied, interview, offer) Automate communication with candidates Ensure compliance with hiring laws Provide visibility to leadership Ads Write job postings that sell the role and company vision Post on relevant job boards and social media A/B test headlines and descriptions Monitor performance of ads (clicks, applications) Adjust spend and targeting for best ROI Applicant Management Keep candidates informed at every stage Collect structured interview notes Score candidates objectively ag

We are seeking a skilled and proactive Project Manager to join our team, responsible for ensuring smooth project execution and improving operational efficiency. Key Responsibilities: • Sprint Planning: Collaborate with Account Managers to update and prioritize sprint tasks in ClickUp, ensure tickets are assigned, and monitor sprint progress. • Daily Standups: Lead team standup meetings, address blockers, and track task completion. • Communication & Task Management: Follow up on unresolved Slack/ClickUp comments and ensure tasks are appropriately actioned. • Enforce Best Practices: Ensure adherence to internal guidelines, such as requiring Loom videos for task reviews, and proactively identify automation opportunities. • Data-Driven Insights: Analyze sprint data and provide recommendations on task prioritization based on team capacity and velocity. • Task Monitoring: Prevent medium/low priority tasks from remaining in the pipeline for prolonged periods. • Stakeholder Collaboration: Work closely with Account Managers to align project goals with client expectations and drive optimal performance. Qualifications: • Proven experience in project management. • Expertise with ClickUp or similar project management tools. • Excellent communication and leadership skills. • Ability to analyze and present data for better sprint outcomes. documents.content: 04/12/2024, 21:02 Automation Specialist Challenge (Longer Version) (Public) 🤖 Automation Specialist Challenge (Longer Version) (Public) Welcome to the onboarding challenge! We are excited to have you onboarded and looking forward to seeing your skills in action. In this challenge, you will find all the necessary information below to get started. Additionally, we have included an overview of the challenge in a video to give you a better understanding of what is expected of you. We understand that this may be a new experience for you, so if you have any questions or concerns, please do not hesitate to reach out to us. We are here to support you and ensure that you have a successful onboarding experience. Good luck, and we look forward to seeing the results of your work! https://impactops.notion.site/Automation-Specialist-Challenge-Longer-Version-Public-56136f20d8174926af01f56bcd0f6dfa 1/4 04/12/2024, 21:02 Automation Specialist Challenge (Longer Version) (Public) Challenge overview Your challenge is to create a lead intake, attribution and call booking system for a client called “Lifespace”. This involves several steps, including 1. Creating a Typeform which would be used to acquire the leads for their upcoming workshop. 2. Setting up automations to populate and update those leads on GoHighLevel, adding them on to Zoom meetings, and populating the data on to Google Sheets 3. documents.name: Customer Success Manager – Goals & Key Performance Indicators.docx
documents.content: Customer Success Manager Goals & Key Performance Indicators Onboarding Onboarding resolution time (from start to completion) under 10 days. Every single client has an onboarding checklist initiated, planned, and fully completed in ClickUp. A task should be included in the checklist so that every 3 days an onboarding status is provided – for example, status update on Slack Canvas on 3rd day, 6th and last day. Offboarding, Client Churn & Winback 35% winback success rate. CSM drives winback strategy formulation, execution and negotiation. 30-day winback plans are planned, completed and tracked on the client’s ClickUp list – applicable for FAM & PPC only. Every single client has an offboarding checklist initiated, planned, and fully completed in ClickUp. Average quarterly qualified client churn rate is 3% or less. Average quarterly unqualified client churn rate is 5% or less. Client Communication 80% of clients meet QC communication standards: daily communication, recurring reports deliverable, etc. If you are managing 10 clients, 8 of them should be meeting the quality controls done on reports delivery, communication on time, etc. The brand managers, graphic designers, strategists, etc. are responsible for meeting the specific QCs, while the CSM is accountable for the overall quality level. Every client has at least 1 monthly call with the CSM. Task has to be tacked on every single client list. Every task when completed needs to indicate the topics covered (e.g. goals status, improvement plan, establishing next month’s goals). Create templated monthly meeting tasks. Client Churn Prevention Client Orientation Average CSAT score is 4 on average and formally measured every quarter. Steps of CSAT process are followed for all client every quarter. This includes measuring satisfaction, gathering what clients love about us, what clients hate about us, and an action plan associated with each feedback loop. ClickUp template to be created. Quarterly improvement plan based on churn reasons, outlining clear actions associated with each main client churn reason. Improvements should be atomic and implemented within 2 weeks. ClickUp plan clearly shows this. Quality Assurance & Compliance Every 2 weeks, each brand has a QC plan that has to be scheduled and completed within these 2 weeks. CSM is accountable for this, while Strategist is responsible. Monthly strategic calls driven by the CSM have to showcase the value of these improvements and goals/KPIs completion. BM & GD team consistently follow the same checklist and best practices, from the definition of a task until peer’s review is done. 80% of BM & GD tasks contain mandatory information and all key fields are completed. 80% of BM & GD deliverables are delivered on the committed deadline. On average, BM & GD tickets don’t stay more than 48 hours on a status. The actual time on 80% of GD tasks meet target effort based on the request time. Monthly service report is presented to Sr leadership showing service key performance indicators Account Growth Average 20% revenue growth per quarter. Example: Client start with 1000 USD. Then we sell one-time services and some other recurring services. At the end of the quarter the client paid us 1500 USD instead of 1000 USD. The revenue growth is 50%, since the initial revenue forecasted at the beginning of the quarter was 1000 USD and the quarter closes with 50% more revenue than initially planned. All Accelerator, PPC and FAM clients have a live upsell plan updated monthly and visible to Sales. Account growth and client journey is part of monthly calls outcomes reflected on ClickUp. Advise which clients we need to let go in order to bring new and better ones.

documents.content: LEADFI AFFILIATE AGREEMENT This Affiliate Agreement (the "Agreement") is entered into as of the date of signing (the "Effective Date"), by and between Momentum Mastery LLC, a Wyoming limited liability company, with its principal address at 1309 Coffeen Ave, Ste 1200, Sheridan, WY 82801 ("Company" or "LeadFi"), and the undersigned affiliate partner ("Affiliate Partner"). Collectively, LeadFi and the Affiliate Partner may be referred to as the "Parties," and individually as a "Party”. This Agreement outlines the terms and conditions for referring potential clients to LeadFi. 1. Affiliate Program Structure and Payment Terms. a. LeadFi offers a two-tier affiliate program designed to compensate affiliate partners for introducing clients to LeadFi services. Affiliate earnings depend on the client’s selected cost-per-lead (“CPL”) rate: i. $3.00 or More Per Lead Clients: a. Tier 1 - Affiliates who directly refer clients paying $3.00 or more per lead earn $0.50 per lead processed. b. Tier 2 - Affiliates who refer another affiliate (who then refers clients paying $3.00 or more per lead) earn $0.15 per lead processed. ii. $2.00-$2.99 Per Lead Clients: a. Tier 1 - Affiliates who directly refer clients paying between $2.00 and $2.99 per lead earn $0.25 per lead processed. b. Tier 2 - Affiliates who refer another affiliate (who then refers clients in this range) earn $0.10 per lead processed. iii. Below $2.00 Per Lead Clients: If a client’s negotiated rate falls below $2.00 per lead, no commissions will be paid. These cases are rare and typically special-rate arrangements where operating margins are minimal and cannot support commission payouts. b. LeadFi charges clients a per-lead fee as outlined above. This fee includes comprehensive financial insights and lead qualification services tailored to each client’s business needs. Affiliate commissions are calculated monthly based on the total number of leads processed within the billing cycle. 2. Payment Schedule. Affiliate payments will be made on a monthly basis, within 15 business days following the end of each month, once the total number of leads processed for the referred clients has been verified. Payments will be made via electronic transfer or another mutually agreed-upon method. 3. Affiliate Tracking. LeadFi will track all referrals through internal tracking systems. Affiliate Partners will be provided with access to track the status and total number of leads processed for their referred clients, ensuring transparency in the affiliate payment process. Page 1 of 5 Doc ID: f80fcb457e3d541340ce99f4389df49427ee00e8 4. Commission Duration. Affiliate commissions shall be paid on a lifetime basis, meaning for as long as the referred client remains an active, paying customer of LeadFi, subject to the terms and limitations below. For purposes of this Agreement, “lifetime” refers to the continuous period during which a referred client maintains an active, paid account with LeadFi and the Affiliate remains in good standing under this Agreement. a. LeadFi’s obligation to pay lifetime commissions is subject to the following limitations: i. receipt of payment from the referred client; ii. refunds, adjustments, or chargebacks related to the referred client; iii. negotiated pricing changes or rate reductions that materially affect profit margins; and iv. the affiliate’s continued compliance with all provisions of this Agreement. b. Notwithstanding the foregoing, lifetime commissions are not guaranteed in perpetuity. In the event the Company undergoes a material ownership change, merger, acquisition, or sale of assets, the Company reserves the right to modify, assign, or terminate this Agreement and any associated affiliate obligations in accordance with the buyout clause below. 5. Buyout Clause. If the Company undergoes significant organizational changes, including but not limited to being sold, acquired, merged, or undergoing any form of ownership change that materially impacts its operations or structure, the Company reserves the right to assign this Agreement to any third party or buy out the Affiliate Partner’s right to commissions. a. In such event, the Affiliate Partner shall be entitled to a buyout based on the estimated future commissions for each referred customer. Future affiliate commissions will be calculated based on the average monthly commission previously earned. The buyout payment will equal the remaining balance owed for each referred customer based on a 12-month period, minus any commissions already paid during that 12-month span. i. Example: If commissions have been paid for six (6) months to the Affiliate Partner, the buyout will be based on the estimated commissions for the remaining six (6) months. b. The total buyout amount shall be paid in equal installments over a six-month term, commencing no later than thirty (30) days after completion of the sale, merger, or acquisition. This clause ensures the Affiliate Partner is fairly compensated for their contributions while preserving the Company’s flexibility during significant ownership or structural changes. 6. Termination. Either Party may terminate this Agreement at any time, upon 30 days’ written notice. Upon termination, any outstanding affiliate payments due to the Affiliate Partner will be paid according to the terms of this Agreement for leads processed prior to the termination date. 7. Pricing Model Flexibility. The Company reserves the right to change its pricing model at any time. Any changes to the pricing model may impact the sales commission percentages provided to Affiliate Partners. If such a change occurs, the commission percentages will be adjusted in accordance with the new pricing model to reflect the updated structure. Any pricing adjustments will be made as part of strategic decisions to better serve the client base, provide more value, improve operations, or enhance Page 2 of 5 Doc ID: f80fcb457e3d541340ce99f4389df49427ee00e8 the profitability of the Company. Affiliate Partners will be notified of any changes in pricing and corresponding adjustments to commissions. Furthermore, the Affiliate understands and agrees that the Company may take any steps determined (in its sole discretion) to address customer issues, sales, support, billing and payment processing that may require adjustments to commissions. This includes but is not limited to any refunds or resolutions implemented for a referred customer that may result in an adjustment to the commissions owed. In this event, the Affiliate Partners will be notified of any changes or adjustments to commissions. 8. Intellectual Property. All intellectual property, data, software, methods, and procedures developed by the Company in connection with the Services, including but not limited to proprietary algorithms, financial evaluation methods, and CRM integration processes, remain the sole property of the Company. 9. Mutual Confidentiality and Non-Circumvention. Both Parties agree not to directly or indirectly circumvent the other Party’s business relationships, contacts, or contracts that may be disclosed or introduced during the term of this Agreement. Each Party further agrees not to attempt to negotiate directly with any of the other Party’s service providers, vendors, partners, or affiliates introduced through this Agreement without prior written consent from the introducing Party. Both Parties acknowledge that a violation of this clause will result in immediate termination of this Agreement. 10. Limitation of Liability. documents.name: Brand Management & Creatives Requests Management.docx
documents.content: Brand Management & Creatives Requests Goal The end goal is to ensure we invoice our clients for Brand Management & Creatives requests in a timely and effective manner. For that purpose, we need to build a system in ClickUp to receive these requests, ensure they are processed by the Finance team and that the team knows when they can go ahead and start working on the request, once the client paid for our service. Currently, this is managed on Slack channels and we are losing track of their requests, and even some are slipping through the cracks. Who opens the request? When the client accepted the service proposition and they want to go ahead with it, the request must be created so that Finance can invoice the client. Once the payment is confirmed, the team can go ahead and work on the request. Requestor: Strategist for ongoing clients / Onboarding Specialist for new clients. Assignee: Finance team. Watcher: should be the person who is waiting on an update on the request to know when they can start working (Brand Managers & Creatives). What information does Finance need to process the request? Previous Monday.com form used. Brand Name Service – Maureen Mc Loughlin to confirm with BMs. Full Page - $1,500+ Main Image Revamp - $250/image & $100/variation image A+ Content Design - $750 Premium A+ Content Design - $1000 Brand Story Design - $500 Storefront Design - $1000 Attach screenshot that shows the client agrees with the price for the request. Extra information included in the form but not required by Finance: Billing Status Complementary (non-billable) Client billed at onboarding. Billable (follow standard pricing). Which countries are the products sold in? Product listing link(s) if already sold on Amazon. Use comma (,) to separate multiple ASINs. If assets aren't included, where should I pull them from: Amazon or website? How many ASINs or variations need to be worked on? List the ASINs or variations. Use comma (,) to separate multiple ASINs. 50 Relevant Keywords Target Audience Indicate gender, age range, etc. Links to the main competitor listings / websites. Use comma (,) to separate the listings/websites. What are the differentiating factors between top competitor and the brand's product? Client's Email. Additional comments or concerns before we start the project. Requested Completion Date. If applicable only. Link to assets. Please include the following brand assets or anything else that might help us with this project. The more, the better. 1. High-quality product image/render (all sides of the product if possible). 2. Brand Logo. 3. Packaging graphics (if any - for nutritional facts, others). 4. Brand Bible (If one exists). 5. Brand Fonts (If available). Mina’s feedback on what the BM team needs to assess a request Billing status. Is budget secured? Has the client paid? We won’t block the request to move forward because client happiness comes first. Track free of charge work. We might want to get a client started with a BM request free of charge. Too many complementary > Raise flag. Client. ASIN. Detailed description of the issue. Request Status New Request Invoice Submitted Payment Collected

documents.name: Reviews. How To Manage Cost Per Message.docx
documents.content: How To Manage Cost Per Message Why do we need to monitor cost per message? The end goal is to deliver the best possible experience to our Reviews customers. Part of that is protecting their budget and ensuring we are making the best out of the investment they make when boosting posts. For this reason, we need to guarantee the average cost per message of their boosted posts is under 5 USD. How do we track the average cost per message? Check the average cost per message daily: - go to the post that is currently Boosted Click on “view insights” Click on “ad” Then you will see the cost per message Register the average cost per message daily in your client’s database. If the average cost per message is around 2 USD, take action. Try different types of designs first. We should have like 5 types of designs for each brand. When you try a design, check if the cost per message decreases, increases or stays the same – around 2 USD. You should aim to find the best performing design, which means, the one that keeps the cost per message lowest. If you cannot keep the cost per message at 2 USD or lower, safely under 5 USD per message, then go and switch the audience. Monitor the situation on daily basis. If the situation improves, keep up the changes you have made. If the cost per message is reaching 5 USD, then pause the boost and inform the client about the situation, to ensure they are happy to continue or offer some options. Ask for support if you need.

These specialists will have Administrator status in 1Password, but only focus on the employees at their specific Owner location. Owners have full administrative privileges Groups and can manage billing, groups, vaults, add and remove team members, and initiate account recovery. Each team has one Owner 1Password comes with three built-in groups by default (the person who created the you can use to delegate administrative team), but additional people can and should responsibilities to your team members. They can be account recovery. The creator of each team shared with some or all team members and is in the Administrators group by default. can be created for a variety of different Additional team members can be added to audiences and purposes. the Administrators group. How to set up 1Password Business in a decentralized organization Many organizations are split into divisions that work completely autonomously. They could be separated by region, area of work, or something else entirely. If your team uses this model, you'll want to approach 1Password in the same way, and assign Site Administrators to each unit. Example use case: You have five distinct business units using 1Password in different geographical sites and would like Administrators for each unit. Instead of using the default Administrators group, you will create separate custom groups for each unit: Owners Site Admins Site Admins Site Admins Site Admins North America Europe APAC LATAM Group #1 Group #1 Group #1 Group #1 Group #1 Group #1 Group #1 Group #1 NA NA Europe Europe APAC APAC LATAM LATAM Vault Vault Vault Vault Vault Vault Vault Vault Vault Vault Vault Vault Workflow steps Create custom groups for each business unit and add the selected Site Administrators Give Site Administrators the desired level of permissions. At minimum, include the permissions Create Vaults and Recovery Develop a vault-creation workflow of your own or follow this commonly used workflow End-user requests the creation of a vault (this can come in an email, ticketing service, etc.) Site Administrators receive that request and collect details to create the vault (For example, the name of the vault, who else should have access, etc.) When the vault is created, the Site Administrator will add the custom group of Site Administrators for that business unit and ensure they have the Manage permission turned on. This is what will allow Site Administrators to make further changes to this vault if needed The Site Administrator who created the vault should now remove themselves as an individual user from the vault. They will still have Administrator privileges because they're part of your account's overarching Site Administrator group, which can manage any vault Add the remaining users or groups to the vault along with the desired permissions. documents.name: Limited-Liability Company Operating Agreement Of Primemate Llc.docx
documents.content: Limited-Liability Company Operating Agreement Of Primemate Llc [STATE OF FORMATION — e.g., Delaware] Effective Date: [EFFECTIVE DATE — MM/DD/YYYY] ARTICLE 1 – ORGANIZATION 1.1 Formation. The Members formed a limited-liability company (“LLC”) by filing a [TYPE OF CHARTER — “Certificate of Formation,” “Articles of Organization,” etc.] with the [FORMATION STATE] Secretary of State on [FORMATION FILING DATE — MM/DD/YYYY]. 1.2 Name & Principal Office. The LLC shall operate as “Primemate LLC.” Principal office: [LLC STREET ADDRESS, CITY STATE ZIP] (or any later location set by the Managers). 1.3 Purpose. To provide Amazon advertising, consulting, and brand-management services and any lawful business related thereto. 1.4 Term. Perpetual unless dissolved under this Agreement or by law. ARTICLE 2 – MEMBERS, OWNERSHIP & CAPITAL 2.1 Capital Contributions. Each Member contributes the property or cash shown in Schedule A and has no further obligation unless all Members agree in writing. 2.2 Capital Accounts & Allocations. Tracked per IRC §704(b); profits and losses allocated pro rata to Percentage Interests. ARTICLE 3 – MANAGEMENT 3.1 Structure. The LLC is member-managed. Each Member is a “Manager.” 3.2 Major Decisions Requiring [SUPERMAJORITY THRESHOLD — e.g., 66⅔ %] Approval: admit new Members, borrow >$[BORROWING CAP], merge, sell substantially all assets, or dissolve. 3.3 Ordinary-Course Authority. Either Manager may bind Primemate in daily operations unless limited by 3.2 or Article 4. ARTICLE 4 – LEAD-ALLOCATION, BRANDING & COLLECTIONS 4.1 Definitions. “Lead” = prospective Amazon-services client routed to Primemate. “Annual Amazon Revenue” = trailing-twelve-month gross Amazon marketplace revenue, proven by acceptable documentation. 4.2 Lead Split. (a) Sub-$1 Million Leads. Annual Amazon Revenue < USD 1,000,000 → handled by Travis Team. (b) ≥ $1 Million Leads. Annual Amazon Revenue ≥ USD 1,000,000 → handled by Trivium Group (Mina Team). 4.3 Ramp-Up Period Use of Trivium Infrastructure. (a) Permitted Branding. During the first [RAMP-UP PERIOD — e.g., 12 months] (the “Ramp-Up Period”) services may be delivered and invoices issued under the Trivium name and through Trivium workspaces and tools. Such use will not violate the Primemate branding covenant. (b) Collections as Agent. Trivium may collect client payments in Trivium’s own name solely as collection agent for Primemate. Funds are deemed Primemate revenue upon receipt and must be (i) recorded in a separate ledger titled “Primemate Client Funds,” and (ii) swept or credited to Primemate’s operating account within [SWEEP PERIOD — e.g., 10 business days]. (c) Visibility Disclosures. All proposals and invoices shall state that “Trivium Group acts on behalf of Primemate LLC.” (d) Books & Audit Rights. Trivium will maintain detailed records of Ramp-Up Period receipts and let Primemate (or its CPA) inspect with [INSPECTION NOTICE — e.g., 5 days] written notice. 4.4 Post Ramp-Up Transition. After the Ramp-Up Period, client-facing materials shift to Primemate branding unless both Members agree otherwise in writing. 4.5 No Diversion. Neither Member may divert or re-brand a Lead (or an existing Primemate client) to an external entity without written consent of the other. 4.6 Classification Disputes. Unresolved disagreements over a Lead’s revenue tier go to binding arbitration under §10.3. ARTICLE 5 – PROFIT-SHARING & SERVICE FEES (Select Option A or Option B, then delete the other.) Option A – Straight Pro Rata 5.1 Net Profits. After operating expenses (including any direct subcontractor costs), Primemate distributes net cash pro rata to Percentage Interests. Option B – Service-Team Fee (Hybrid) 5.1 Service Fee. The servicing Team first receives a fee = [FEE % — e.g., 30 %] of gross collected revenue from its Leads; remaining net profits then split pro rata. 5.2 Tax Distributions. Quarterly, the LLC distributes cash to cover each Member’s tax on allocated income, using the highest combined marginal rate not exceeding [MAX MARGINAL RATE — e.g., 40 %]. ARTICLE 6 – TAX ELECTION & WITHHOLDING 6.1 The LLC will be taxed as a [TAX CLASSIFICATION — “partnership,” “S corporation (upon Form 2553 filing),” etc.]. [RESPONSIBLE MEMBER NAME] is authorized to sign returns and any election forms. 6.2 The LLC may withhold amounts required by law from distributions. ARTICLE 7 – TRANSFER & BUY-SELL 7.1 Restrictions. No Member may Transfer any Interest without either unanimous written consent or compliance with Schedule B (Buy-Sell). 7.2 Triggering Events: death, disability > 90 days, voluntary withdrawal, felony conviction, or bankruptcy. ARTICLE 8 – CONFIDENTIALITY, IP & NON-COMPETE 8.1 Confidentiality. Members shall keep Primemate and client information confidential, even when stored on the Trivium Slack workspace. 8.2 IP Ownership. All work product created while servicing Primemate clients is Primemate property, regardless of which workspace or logo appears. 8.3 Limited Non-Compete. For 12 months after a Member’s withdrawal, that Member shall not solicit Primemate clients outside the revenue band he previously serviced without written consent of the other. ARTICLE 9 – DISSOLUTION & DISPUTES 9.1 Dissolution Triggers: unanimous consent, sale of all assets, court decree, or impossibility. 9.2 Wind-Up. Assets liquidated, liabilities paid, reserves set, remainder distributed per capital accounts. 9.3 Dispute Resolution. 30-day good-faith negotiation → binding arbitration under AAA Commercial Rules in [ARBITRATION CITY & STATE]; each side bears its own costs. 9.4 Governing Law, Amendments, Counterparts, E-Signatures. SCHEDULE A – CAPITAL CONTRIBUTIONS SCHEDULE B – BUY-SELL TERMS (Short-Form) Price = Fair Market Value of the departing Interest, determined by independent appraiser mutually selected within 30 days. Payment = 20 % cash at closing; balance via 36 equal monthly installments at 8 % simple interest. Right of First Refusal in favor of the non-transferring Member before any third-party sale. documents.name: Culture Index _ ClickUp Integration v2.docx
documents.content: Culture Index & ClickUp Integration 1. Business Goal & Core Objective Ensure the integration speeds up identifying who is (and isn’t) a match based on their Culture Index profile. Minimize manual data-checking to free recruiters’ time for more strategic tasks. Automate rejections of poor fits and expedite moving strong fits to interviews. 2. Culture Index Overview & Position Links Unique Applicant Links Each specific position (e.g., “Director of Operations”) has its own dedicated Culture Index survey link. If a candidate uses that link, you automatically know which position they applied for. Requirement: The integration must capture which link/survey/position was used, so the correct role is mapped in ClickUp. General (All Positions) Link If someone uses the “All Positions” link, the Culture Index data won’t automatically include the role. Requirement: The system must handle this scenario—storing that the role is unknown or “unassigned” and alerting the recruiting team to manually assign it. 3. Candidate Sources LinkedIn Candidates typically fill a ClickUp form and are then redirected to Culture Index. Requirement: As soon as the ClickUp form is submitted, a candidate task is created in ClickUp—even if the candidate does not complete the Culture Index right away Headhunters External recruiters may submit candidates via a separate ClickUp form. Requirement: The system should capture the recruiter’s name (source) to track the pipeline properly. Referrals / Manual Entries Candidates can also be referred or manually added to ClickUp. Requirement: The system must still be able to match them to Culture Index data if/when they complete a survey. 4. ClickUp Folder & List Setup Recruiting Pipeline Set Up: Each open position has its own “List” within the “Recruiting Pipelines” folder in ClickUp. Requirement: The system must correctly place or move candidate tasks into the right list (i.e., the right open role) based on the data from Culture Index or from the submitted form. Custom Fields ClickUp uses custom fields such as “Culture Index,” “Culture Index Result,” “Source,” etc. Requirement: All Culture Index data (drive, social, patience, detail, energy units, innovation, logic, Culture Index (e.g. Philosopher)) must be automatically populated in these fields or new fields if needed. 5. Culture Index Data Points to Sync Primary CI Fields Drive (A), Social (B), Patience (C), Detail (D), Energy Units (EU), Logic (L), Innovation (I). A, B, C, D are relative to the red baseline; EU, L, I are absolute values. Requirement: The integration must calculate the relative scores for A, B, C, D and label them (e.g., slightly high, high, extremely high, slightly low, etc.) based on thresholds. Scoring Logic For A, B, C, D: if (score >= -0.2 && score <= 0.2) return “0”; if (score > 0.2 && score <= 1.99) return “Slightly High”; if (score > 1.99 && score <= 2.99) return “High”; if (score > 2.99) return “Extremely High”; if (score < -0.2 && score >= -1.99) return “Slightly Low”; if (score < -1.99 && score >= -2.99) return “Low”; if (score < -2.99) return “Extremely Low”; Absolute numbers (L and I: 0–10, EU: 0–100). Requirement: Implement or maintain a function that calculates these relative values and maps them to the correct label. Reflect absolute numbers too. 6. Real-Time or Near-Real-Time Updates Event-Driven or Frequent Sync As soon as a candidate completes or updates their Culture Index, ClickUp should reflect it without manual refresh. Requirement: Use the Culture Index API (if available) to push updates to ClickUp in real-time or at frequent intervals (as frequently as possible). Minimizes delay so recruiters can act on new data immediately. 7. Candidate Workflow in ClickUp No Response Handling Candidates move from New Candidate to Culture Index Test when they have not completed the Culture Index survey. As long as they stay in the Culture Index survey, they will receive up to 4 follow up. If a candidate doesn’t complete CI within 7 days, they must move to a “No Response” status. Right now, a person is checking daily if someone needs to move out from Culture Index Test if they filled out their response, or keep them there if they haven’t. Requirement: Automate check-ins/reminders and detect non-responders to update status –review current automation in ClickUp. 8. Handling Missing Candidates in ClickUp Candidate Not Found in ClickUp A Culture Index entry might come in for someone who never filled the ClickUp form. Requirement: Automatically create a new candidate record in ClickUp or flag it for review, so the recruiting team can verify the correct role/source. Position Not Specified If a candidate used the general CI link, they might not have selected a specific role. Requirement: Integration notes “Unassigned role” or “Unknown” so that a recruiter can manually assign it. 9. Documentation & Training End-User Guide Clear instructions for recruiters to understand how the integration works, what data fields mean, and what is automated vs. manual. Requirement: Provide a straightforward user manual or training videos for the Operations. Technical Maintenance Guide Documentation for the tech team to maintain or modify the integration: environment setup, API keys, data mapping, error handling steps. Requirement: Keep a living document that can be updated as new roles or disqualification rules are added. 10. Error Handling & Logging Common Failure Points Culture Index API unavailability or timeouts. Mismatched data (e.g., name/email mismatch) resulting in missing candidate records. Bulk updates or partial data updates failing. Automated email sending errors (spam flags, etc.). Requirement: The integration must log errors clearly (e.g., in a spreadsheet, a ticketing system, or Slack notifications) and attempt retries if feasible. ops-admin@triviumco.com or a Slack channel must be used to inform errors that need admin attention. Fallback / Manual Override The system must allow recruiters or the tech team to override or correct any incorrect data or statuses. Requirement: Provide a clear process for manual corrections if automated logic is incorrect. 11. Testing & Validation Unit & Integration Testing Test each step: user submission → Culture Index completion → real-time data sync → field population in ClickUp → auto disqualification. Requirement: Comprehensive test scripts to ensure correct data handling at each stage. User Acceptance Testing (UAT) HR/recruiters run the workflow end-to-end with a few test candidates. Requirement: Final sign-off after verifying all statuses, email automations, and data fields are correct. 12. Implementation & Technical Considerations Culture Index API Confirm endpoints, authentication, data format (JSON/XML), and event-driven push vs. scheduled pull. Requirement: Securely store and handle any API credentials. Ensure compliance with the Culture Index usage terms. Use 1Password’s Operations vault. ClickUp API or Native Automations Possibly use webhooks, or third-party tools (Zapier, Make/Integromat, etc.). Requirement: Decide on the best approach for stable, maintainable, and real-time integration. Google Suite Integration Trium uses Google Suite—there could be email triggers, Google Sheets logging, etc. Requirement: Confirm if any part of the process (like error logging) is best handled in Google Sheets or if everything remains in ClickUp. 14. Automatic Disqualification Criteria To be implemented only after the information from the Culture Index is reliably and consistently flowing into ClickUp Culture Index Result Possible statuses (manual now but must be automated once the integration proves to be reliable): Pass (good fit) Not a good fit Needs to take (no survey found) / Needs to retake (invalid or incomplete). Requirement: After evaluating a candidate’s A/B/C/D/L/I/EU, automatically assign a “Pass” or “Not a good fit” or keep them in “Needs to take/retake.” Example of Current Disqualification Criteria: Example given: If A (drive) is to the lef

documents.content: Online Seller Solutions Onboarding Program 07-11-23 Amazon Content 07-11-23 Amazon Deep Dive Seller Central and Ideal Customer This section provides comprehensive insights into various aspects of Amazon. For individuals seeking additional information or undergoing onboarding for roles like Account Manager, we recommend referring to the Appendix section in this file for more detailed content. 3 Amazon Specific Onboarding This section encompasses all the training essential for your success at Online Seller Solutions. Depending on your role, you may delve deeper into specific knowledge areas. Our goal is to provide tailored, comprehensive training, ensuring that you have the expertise needed to excel professionally. Your success is our priority, and we are committed to empowering you with the skills necessary to thrive in your role at Online Seller Solutions. Selling on Amazon Amazon Marketplace Amazon Marketplace is an e-commerce platform that allows third-party sellers to sell on Amazon. Amazon Marketplace is so wholly integrated into Amazon that if we were to make a Venn diagram, the circles would overlap. Amazon Seller Central Amazon Seller Central is the interface that is used by merchants to market and sell their products directly to customers within the Amazon Marketplace. An Amazon Seller Central account is considered a marketplace or third-party Amazon seller (3P). The Amazon seller is responsible for setting up and maintaining their seller account. ASIN Amazon Standard Identification Number (ASIN) is a ten-digit alphanumeric code that identifies products on Amazon. It’s unique for each product and is assigned when you create a new product in Amazon’s catalog. Almost every product on Amazon has an ASIN with the exception of books (they use the ISBN or International Standard Book Number in place of an ASIN). Getting this Amazon identifier for your products is necessary before you can sell them on Amazon. UPC Code Unique Product Codes (UPC) are 12-digit codes that are used to identify retail products. They are usually accompanied by a barcode that can be scanned for quick identification. This is the most common code used in the US, Canada, the UK, and Australia. SKU An SKU (stock-keeping unit) is a specific merchant's product identifier. The SKU is a critical piece of data in every inventory file that you submit to us. Amazon uses the SKUs in your inventory file to associate your products with the appropriate product detail page in our catalog (if one already exists). Catalog 07-11-23 Catalog: Amazon Listing Amazon listing - An Amazon product listing is the product page for each of the items that are going to be sold on Amazon. It is made up of the information you enter when you list your product including its title, images, description, and price. Shoppers on Amazon use product listing pages to make a purchase, i.e. the Add to Cart button is on all product listing pages. As a result, getting the product listing right will determine the success of your products on Amazon. 1. What an Amazon Product Listing Does? An Amazon product listing performs several functions, but the two main ones are: ● Enables your products to be found in Amazon searches. ● Encourages shoppers to purchase your products. 2. Essential Elements of an Amazon Product Listing ● Product title: your product title in an Amazon product listing can be up to 500 characters (with some products you get 250 characters). You should include the main keyword for the product as close to the start of the title as possible. You should also include all the main elements such as brand, product name, model number, color, size, type, etc. ● Images: an Amazon product listing should have at least five images of the product. Showing multiple angles of the product and its packaging is also helpful. In addition, it is important to follow Amazon's requirements for images. ● Bullet points: below the price, product options, and shipping details of an Amazon product listing page are several bullet points. The best way to use this section is to highlight the product's main features and benefits. ● Description: even though a description is not as important as bullet points, it is still important. It lets you give more information about the product and include your keywords again. When writing your product description, think about your customer. What is the information they would most want to know? This is the information you should include. Catalog: Amazon Listing 3. Optimization - A product listing is more than a way of getting your products onto the Amazon marketplace. Product listings are also a tool you can use to increase your sales. The use of keywords in the listing is essential for the positioning of the product. 4. Backends Sellers can improve the ranking of their products on organic searches by approaching the matter from both sides in the detail page of a listing and backend keywords. Here we mention a few guidelines to optimize and fill the search terms keywords of a listing. ● Stay under the length limit. (ideally under 249 bytes) ● You can use all lowercase. ● Separate words with spaces. ● Don't repeat words within the Search Terms field. ● Don't include your brand or other brand names in Search Terms. ● Don't include ASINs in Search Terms ● No temporary statements such as "new" or "on sale now." ● Don't add abusive or offensive terms. The blank spaces don't count when amazon measures the bytes of the Search Terms field. Catalog: Amazon Listing 5. Suppressed listings - Suppressed listings usually occur when a specific product listing doesn’t quite live up to Amazon’s rigorous standards. According to Amazon, these suppression guidelines are in place to make it easier for consumers to locate, research, and actually purchase products on its platform. In order to ensure product listings won’t be suppressed by Amazon, sellers should include all required product details and information. Common examples of missing or insufficient information that can lead to suppressed listings include: ● Any product listing without at least one main image. ● Any listing (excluding certain categories such as apparel, books, or shoes) without a detailed product description. ● Any clothing or accessories item with a title longer than 80 characters. ● Any product listing without a defined category type. Catalog: Variations Variations - Amazon product variations allow brands to show multiple variations of the same product to shoppers. By adding product variations to your Amazon listings, you improve the shopping experience for your customers. 1. Elements of a family variation Before creating a variation, sellers must understand the three main components that make an ASIN parent-child relationship work: Without any of these entities, a family variation won't show on the product detail page. Parent ASIN: This ASIN is a non-buyable entity, meaning that it is not attached to a product or product ID and doesn't hold any inventory. Its only purpose is to link the child ASINs together and provide attributes like title and description to the listing. Amazon uses the parent ASINs as the link between the products in a variation. Once a parent's ASIN is deleted, the family falls apart and each child's ASIN will show on a separate detail page. Child ASIN: These are the products inside of a family that are linked to each other by the parent ASIN, every child corresponds to a different variation of the product (different size, color, flavor, etc) Variation theme: This sets and defines the characteristic(s) that differ in the product line. The theme is what Amazon uses to catalog the type of variation. It can be single or double and varies between categories. For example in the clothing category, a variation theme can be color this is a single variation because the only thing that changes between the lines is the color of the item. documents.name: QC Audits Process Guide.docx
documents.content: This guide outlines the Quality Control (QC) Audit process for different services, including PPC, PPC Accelerator, Full Management, and PPC Launchpad. Follow these steps to ensure that each audit is thorough and meets the required standards. General Preparation Access the Audit Tracker: Open the "Client Slack Audit Tracker v2" file. Navigate to the Main Database and copy data from columns L to O. Paste this data into the 'Audits by Jazz and Dia' sheet. Filter the Date: Filter the data to show entries for today's date. Fill in the required details in Column F and Column G as per the date. Refer to the Guidelines: Open the Audit Guidelines and Audit Plan sheets to identify specific requirements for each channel or brand being audited. Part 1 - PPC Audits Select a Brand: Search a brand channel (e.g., "Numa Foods") on Slack. Check Daily Updates: For each brand, confirm that the Data Analyst has sent the previous day's update to the channel. If an update has been sent, mark it as Complete. Review Unanswered Messages: Check the channel and its threads for any unanswered client inquiries or messages. If all inquiries are addressed, mark the audit as Complete. Verify Onboarding Channels: For channels still in the onboarding phase, ensure that the Strategist has sent the necessary onboarding updates. Part 2 - FAM/Accelerator/Other Services Audits Audit PPC Accelerator and Full Management Channels: Similar to PPC, check that daily updates are sent and no messages are left unanswered. Example: For "Misumi Skincare," verify that the daily update is present and mark it as Complete if all requirements are met. Tagging Missed Updates: If updates are missing, tag the responsible Strategist in the Trivium QC Audits channel. Include an FYI to the PPC Team to notify them of the missed update. Audit Creatives, Reviews, and DSP Services: For these services, ensure that weekly updates (usually on Mondays) are sent and that no client messages are left unanswered. If updates or responses are missing, tag the appropriate team in the QC Audits channel. Part 3 - PPC Launchpad Audits Schedule for Weekly Update Checks: Every Thursday, check if a weekly update was sent on Wednesday to the PPC Launchpad channel. Verify that all updates were sent, and if so, mark them as Complete. Check for Unanswered Messages: Review the channel for any unanswered client messages. If all inquiries have been addressed, mark the audit as Complete. Check the Opt-Out Sheet: Before performing audits, verify the Opt-Out Sheet to identify any clients who opted out of receiving updates. Do not tag strategists for missed updates if the client has opted out. Daily and Weekly Schedule for QC Audits Monday: Review Friday updates. Tuesday: Review Monday updates, which should include an Action Plan description and a link to the Action Plan on ClickUp. Wednesday: Review Tuesday updates. Thursday: Review Wednesday updates. Friday: Review Thursday updates. Monthly Schedule for QC Audits On the 5th of every month, a message with the Monthly Action Plan should be posted for each PPC client, including a link to the Action Plan on ClickUp. This Monthly Action Plan should written according to the following template. Hey client I wanted to present to you a 30-60 day game plan so you’re aware of exactly what the team and I are working on for each product. I’m going to cover both advertising things as well as other brand related items I might suggest you handle. Scaling: for product A I plan to take the current adspend from x to y in an effort to grow revenue. I will monitor growth carefully and make sure we aren’t over spending For product B, same as above. The goal is to go from x to y spending while not dropping below a Z ROAS Optimization: for product C, I’m going to focus now on growing profit. We are spending x and profit is y per week. The goal is to try and get up to x in profit. Maintenance for product D, right now we are spending x at a y ROAS. I’m going to let it stabilize here and focus on the other products for now. Brand improvements Below is a list of things we can do to improve the results of the brand product A: optimize listing images. This can be done by us or you. Ideally this month. This will increase CVR which will make our ads more profitable and us generate more revenue overall Product B: get more reviews. Right now we only have x reviews at y star rating. If we improved that to xx reviews and yy star rating, our CTR and CVR would improve a lot making us a lot more profit with current marketing efforts Product C: updating and optimizing SEO. This can be done by us or you. Let’s shoot to get it done this month. This will help us index better on Amazon and the ads will perform better as well as us gaining better organic rankings Known approved exceptions for this process: Precision Pro - quarterly updates until April 2025. This QC Audits guide ensures that each channel and service is monitored for timely updates and responses, maintaining high-quality communication with clients. Make sure to mark tasks as Complete only when all criteria are met.

When the housekeeper is done, perform a walkthrough and spot check for dust and dirty spots in the house to ensure everything is clean and organzied - When the PA is done, perform a walkthrough and spot check to ensure all meal preps are sealed and weight correctly. - Review the household supplies list with the PA and submit the shopping list to Brandy for purchase - Process payment to housekeeper through Mina's Zelle or Venmo account | Weekly | On Site Check in with Mina about his first meal - always check with Mina what he want to eat first | - take a lightly damp papertowel and microwave the pre-portioned meal in the microwave at 1000W for 1 minute - lightly toss the salad green with olive oil and a dash of salt - plate the chicken and rice on a dinner plate with the dressed green salad and a side sauce (if available) - serve the lunch plate with main fork and main knife with papernapkin to Mina either at the dining table or at his desk - on a small plate, put together half banana, sliced, with some chocolates (if available) with his daily supplements (check with Mina) | Daily | On Site At 2pm-3pm - check in with Mina for his second coffee or caffeine drink of the day | Daily | On Site At 3pm - 4pm Check in with Mina about his second meal - always check with Mina what he want to eat first | - take a lightly damp papertowel and microwave the pre-portioned meal in the microwave at 1000W for 1 minute - lightly toss the salad green with olive oil and a dash of salt - plate the chicken and rice on a dinner plate with the dressed green salad and a side sauce (if available) - serve the lunch plate with main fork and main knife with papernapkin to Mina either at the dining table or at his desk - on a small plate, put together half banana, sliced, with some chocolates (if available) with his daily supplements (check with Mina) | Daily | On Site 5pm - Do last check-in with Mina for tomorrow's tasks (i.e. package pickup or in person errands) | Daily | Both Packing bags for Mina | Packing step 1 - put together packing list using the standard formats (long trip vs. weekend trip) - always check the weather and the occasion he is going to " Packing step 2 - review the packing list with Brandy and Mina, revise the list with feedbacks from them "Packing step 3 - purchase any items needed for the trip (i.e. travel toiletries refill, special occasion outfit (wedding) /costumes, pharmacy supplies and supplements), this should be done at least 3 days before the packing - check necessary attire for wedding - drop off any dry cleaning at least one week before the travel date" "Packing step 4 - 2 days before the trip, pickout the clothes, shoes, sunglasses, toiletries, supplements and lay it out for Mina and Brandy to review and approve - Do not pack Mina's backpack, he does this on his own. " "Packing step 5 - 1 day before the trip, charge his technologies - Whoop watch - Anker battery pack - macbook pro - mouse - airpod - travel electric shaver " "Packing step 6 - 2 days before the trip, pack the approved clothes / shoes / supplements / toiletries in his suitcase by order of day - for example, for a weekend trip, Sunday outfits should go in first (i.e. at the bottom of the suitcase), follows by Saturday outfits in the middle and finally Friday's outfits on top " "Packing step 7 - Once the suitcase is pack, go through the packing organization and outfit with Mina for the last time - once Mina give the final approval, zip up the suitcase and leave it by the front door for Mina to grab on his way out " "Packing step 8 - One the day of their departure, check with Brandy and Mina to toss any perishable food in the fridge - take out the trash - turn off all humidifers in the apartment - general house cleaning - pick up mail from mailbox" Unpacking bags for Mina | Unpacking step 1 - schedule the housekeeper and PA to come to the apartment on the day after of Mina's return from a trip. Unpacking step 2 - 72 hours before they return from the trip, confirm with the housekeeper and PA for their arrival time for the day after "Unpacking step 3 - housekeeper's tasks - to wash all travel clothes - change the bedding to fresh bedsheet / pillow case and duvet cover (if needed) - clean out the fridge and toss any expired or rotten perishables - wipe down the fridge shelves - perform general housekeeping tasks as normal" "Unpacking step 4 - PA's tasks - unpack all travel clothes and give them to the housekeeper to wash - unpack the toiletries bag and replace any items that are running low, alert Mina and Brandy if a purchase is needed - repack the toiletries bag with full items, put the toiletries bag back into the suitcase - charge the travel electric shaver - unpack the supplement bag and replace any items that are running low, alert Mina and Brandy if a purchase is needed - repack thesupplement bag with full items, put the supplement bag back into the suitcase - unpack Mina's technologies and charge them: Whoop watch / Anker battery pack / macbook pro / mouse / airpod - unpack his shoes and put them back to his closest - wipe down suitcase (inside and out) if it is dirty - put suitcase back to the closest - ready for the next trip - feedback loop - ask for Mina's feedback on the packing for this specific trip and adjust SOP accordingly" Manage Household Inventory Supplies | Household Inventory Supplies step 1 - PA tasks - On Monday, the PA should go through each room and check for household inventories - All bathrooms should have refill and backup in the drawers (i.e. toilet paper, toiletries supplies for visiting guests, femine products, scent refill, etc) - All full bathrooms should have fresh towels (face and body and floormat) - All bedrooms should have an extra set of bed linen in the closest - Beverage Fridge should have a selection of water bottles, sparkling water, mixers (tonic and ginger beer), energy drink, popi soda, etc. - Snack Drawer should have a selection of chocolate snacks for Mina, jerky, chips, candies, mixed nuts, etc - Laundry Room should have minimum a half full bottle of detergent and a half full bottle of softerner, multiples clean mop head, etc - Follow daily login routine | Log into all required systems at the start of the shift. | https://app.trainual.com/ac4310f4-4b3b-416a-8acb-251007300ec7/courses/5119677/consume Follow opening procedures | Prepare front desk, systems, and space for the day. Follow closing procedures | Close out systems, secure workspace, and complete end-of-day tasks. Navigating GoHighLevel | Understand how to move confidently through the dashboard, conversations, contacts, calendars, tasks, and pipelines so you can manage leads and appointments efficiently without missing activity. Navigating BLVD | Know how to view the provider calendar, confirm appointment details, check availability, and ensure all booked appointments are accurately reflected. Calling from Lead Connector (GHL) | Place outbound calls directly from GoHighLevel using Lead Connector so all call attempts are automatically logged under the contact record. Receiving calls from Ring Central | Answer inbound calls, access the caller’s record quickly, and log any important notes or follow up actions inside GoHighLevel immediately during/after the call. "Speed to Lead" Rule and updating Slack | All new leads must be contacted within 5 minutes during business hours to maximize booking rates and show responsiveness. Add a comment as soon as possible to the proper Slack notification. This way the team is aware you are handling the lead. Knowledge of treatments and promotional pricing | Have a clear understanding of each treatment, current promotions, pricing structure, deposits, and packages so you can confidently answer questions and position the best option. Booking an appointment on GoHighLevel | Schedule the consultation under the correct contact profile and calendar, confirm date and time verbally, ensure all details are accurate, and communicate directions, deposit information, and pre visit instructions before ending the call. Creating a contact in GoHighLevel | Properly enter full name, phone number, email, and lead source so every prospect is tracked correctly for follow up and reporting. Sending the deposit link in GoHighLevel | Apply the correct payment tag so the system automatically generates and sends the secure invoice via text and email. Taking a deposit payment over the phone Selecting a provider when booking an appointment | Choose the correct nurse or provider based on availability, treatment type, and any special scheduling notes. Extending an treatment time in the calendar Adding a booked appointment to BLVD after it is made in GoHighLevel | Immediately mirror every confirmed appointment from GoHighLevel into BLVD to ensure the provider’s clinical calendar is accurate. Adding a screenshot of the BLVD appointment into Slack | Upload proof of the scheduled appointment in Slack for internal confirmation and accountability. Creating a task in GoHightLevel | Set follow up tasks for callbacks, reschedules, pending deposits, or undecided leads so no opportunity is forgotten. Adding notes and internal comments in GoHighLevel | Document key details from conversations including objections, concerns, preferences, and next steps so anyone on the team can pick up seamlessly. How to navigate conversations in GoHighLevel | Use the conversations tab to manage SMS, email, missed calls, and social messages while keeping communication organized and timely. Sending a text snippet in GoHighLevel | Use approved pre saved message templates to maintain brand consistency and ensure accurate information is being sent. Sending before & afters in GoHighLevel | Send approved before and after images when appropriate to educate and build trust, always matching the treatment discussed. Clearing the inboxes in GoHighLevel | Keep all inboxes as close to empty as possible by responding, assigning, or closing conversations daily so no lead is left unattended.
