documents.content: Trivium 12/5 Consistent Issues: Reporting Slack Notifications There has been multiple conversations had with everyone on the team, the trainings, and the training recordings not being rewatched. The consistent issues you’re having are derived from this. Adoption Issues which affect the reporting you are seeing. We built the system to be used in a specific way. When it is not properly used, the reports will not populate correctly. It is imperative that your team uses the methods that were trained on in order for the system to automate and report correctly. Example and issues below. Your team is booking closing calls outside of the “approved booking links” that were trained on. The result of that will be 1) none of the automations we built based off of that trigger will fire 2) None of the reporting that we built will recognize the call that was had as a closing call. Here shows an example of what happens when a booked call happens outside of the links we gave. You can see below that the meeting type is not recognized. Additionally, you can see in the other screenshot that the approved booking links have been used 0 times. Which is why the reporting you are looking at feels incorrect. Images DM’d to Ryan on Dec 4 This is closing call outcomes for this month. So this is only Dec 1-4. If you hover over the blue bars, it will show you the stages and number of total bookings. Again, this only works when the team is using the approved booking links listed in the image above. Any bookings outside of those links will not report. “Here all of our closers are having a ton of disco calls that are actually closing calls and its not reflected” This is tracking to the same issue. They are not using the proper booking links. That’s what dictates closing vs disco calls. “Setter numbers are off. Last week Kobi set 21 calls” This report isn’t showing how many calls were booked by Kobi. This is showing how many leads were assigned to him and how many calls he made to those leads. “This is using an all time value. I don't think that makes sense” This report has been adjusted to reflect the current quarter. However, keep in mind that the data will only report accurately if the sales team is using the pipeline properly. “Why are these disco calls missing revenue details?” This information is gathered through a form submission or your team inputting this information. If it is not there, it is because it was not filled out on the form. This could be related to the number of forminator forms that may not have this property information on there. In order to address this, your team would need to look at this property in the future and fill it out or it needs to be on the forms. It is also now a required entry when moving a deal into the discovery call qualified stage. This requires your team to move deals properly which has been an issue to this point. Manfredo54@gmail.com entered the system on 10/10 from Calendly. He was an old lead that booked. “Deal stage updates still has 100 updates a day it crazy. Makes the channel useless” This is the core of Triviums issues right now with new system adoption. This channel getting this many notifications per day is a red flag that they are not using the system properly and moving their deals. IF the team was properly using the system, this channel would have 0 notifications. This channel is made for you and the management team to see that the sales team is not properly using the system. The reason why Khalid Alasedi is still showing in this pipeline is because he was never moved to “discovery call complete qualified” which would have removed the tag and not sent this notification. Instead, your team is skipping steps and dropping them into redzone, once again causing issues in your system. This was fixed yesterday. If you look in the channel: After Harrison's test submission, the rest have come in the same. When you came to us to update your system, you were frustrated because your data integrity was a mess and there was no standardization. We have built a very simple system for your team that will deliver exactly what you asked for. For that to happen, the team needs to follow the standardized process we put in place. There are no tweaks/changes/updates that we can make that will solve this issue if the sales team continues to do what they want. Every tweak we make from here on out would further complicate the system built. The only way for this to work is for Plamy, as sales manager, to hold the team accountable for following the process. She should be following the #deal-stage-updates like a hawk and forcing the team to follow the process. Maureen should not be looking to make changes at this time. She should be focused on understanding how the system works in order to help guide Plamy and the team towards full system adoption. Aaron and Harrison are no longer involved in the build process. Everything should be directed to Hunter at this point. We have spent a lot of time doing extra work that was out of scope (cleanup, additional OOS items, impromptu meetings). As far as the channel, there are multiple instances where the same issue has arisen and the exact same solution has been presented. It is all leading back to user error from the sales team. In the past, with clients who have had issues with system adoptions, we’ve seen commission docked/not paid on deals that have not been moved through the system properly. In reality, the team not following through with the system that you invested money in is causing you to not focus on what moves your business forward. Without their buy-in, you are unable to see the important numbers for your business’ health (revenue, booked calls, closing %, etc.). Until they adopt, you will not be able to make any data driven decisions. If this were me, as CEO, I would make sure my sales manager understands the process front to back and is holding the sales team accountable in whatever way you see fit. documents.content: Sales Rep Pro Tools Resources Document Use this resource to access all the materials associated with this workshop Login to HubSpot Connect Email Inbox KB article on how to connect your email inbox to HubSpot Install HubSpot Sales Extension KB article on how to download and install the HubSpot sales extension HubSpot Sales Hub Tutorial For Beginners (2024) Differences between saved views, active lists, and static lists Learn about the different ways you can segment your contacts in your HubSpot account: saved filters, active lists, and static lists. Combine lists Learn how to set the list criteria of a new list to combine the contacts included in two or more of your existing lists. View and filter lists Learn how to create save views for lists. Customize list columns You can customize the columns displayed in lists by clicking the Actions dropdown menu and selecting Edit columns. Export your lists Learn how to export an active or static list of your contacts and their associated companies. Add or remove records from a list Learn how to add or remove contacts from a list. My name is [Your Name], and I’m the Operations Associate and Slack Channel Manager. I’m here to support you as we get started and help make great things happen together! My role is to ensure everything runs smoothly and that you feel fully supported as we get started. Over the next few days, we’ll guide you through a few simple steps to get everything set up. One of the first steps will be confirming your preferred billing method so we can finalize your account on our end. We offer two secure, pull-based payment options for your monthly subscription: ACH or Credit Card. Options for Submitting Payments: ACH Authorization We'll send you a PandaDoc form, just sign it to authorize ACH payments from your bank account. Credit Card via Authorize You can securely authorize a one-time $0.10 charge to save your info. This is the final step before we can officially get started and introduce you to your Fulfillment Team. Just a reminder, these are our payment options: ACH Authorization We'll send you a PandaDoc form, just sign it to authorize ACH payments from your bank account. Credit Card via Authorize You can securely authorize a one-time $0.10 charge to save your info. Use the PandaDoc agreement or this direct link [INSERT HYPERLINK] Pay Online via Invoice You’ll receive an invoice, follow the steps below to pay online: • Click here [HYPERLINK] to pay online • Choose: “ACH/eCheck” or “Credit Card” • Enter your info and submit your payment Once this is completed, we’ll be able to finalize your account and schedule your Welcome Call so we can get started on your brand’s strategy! Please let me know if you have any questions or if there's anything I can help with. Looking forward to moving ahead! Best regards,

Note: I received an email right away that said this after I selected 0-80k sales /mo : Hi Katya Vass, Thank you for your interest in Envision Horizons. After reviewing your company's current presence on Amazon, we are unfortunately unable to extend our services in a way that would drive maximum value. As a firm focused on sustainable growth for Amazon brands, we require a high revenue threshold for our specialized services to realize full return on investment. If you think you have received this email in error, and/or you would like to discuss Envision Horizons services further, I would be happy to set up a call to discuss alternative solutions. Please reply to this email a few times within the next week that you are free and I will get back to you as soon as I can! | Inquiry form / free marketing plan: https://www.loom.com/share/2b30bc506fc34dfebdb01b771a052115?sid=e0dac31c-6044-4590-ba3b-55062ae8ce26 | Inquiry form: https://www.loom.com/share/cb81f56685304b6b861c2cab4eb4a2b0?sid=a128fd30-482e-43a5-a7ac-d294432c73cd What do you like about this customer journey? | What I liked about the landing page: phone number top right, I felt more trust by recognizing their clients, the flow of the page from top to bottom matched my thought process and questions: 1. What do they do 2. Who else trusts this company? 3. What is their process and expertise? 4. Case study 5. Other publications highlighting this service | homepage tour / scroll: https://www.loom.com/share/a046ab1dc18d47b2b3774ff2bf96cffe?sid=230b3720-0623-402c-ad3a-bb16607c4903. Compared to the Amazon Guy, this site didn't feel approachable or like there was a human touch to it (very word driven). The video on the top of the page did help with creating trust. | homepage tour / scroll: https://www.loom.com/share/69cdfb656542407bbb990191896cdb29?sid=44df101b-a870-453e-aa56-4847d1505781. Overall, I loved this site. I felt it was visually engaging and had a similar flow to MAG, where my thought process as a potential customer was predicted and followed (what is the USP / special results they've acheived, what other brands am I familiar with who are using this company, case studies with exact results). Breaking down the case study on the homepage (not just "see more here" was a plus). | I enjoyed the customer journey and felt that the website was easy to navigate and they created trust by showing not only other faces but also highlighting other brands they've worked with. One USP that I hadn't seen featured yet was them talking about how their clients are raising funding and getting acquired after their efforts. | The website is clean and they have big brands as clients. Compared to Klient Boost, I didn't feel the same understanding of their brand and what makes them unique. I like to see actual numbers and attention-grabbing data. It felt AI heavy and not personal What don't you like about this customer journey? | It looked very trustworthy (lots of faces and social proof) and I felt comfortable with proceeding to the free audit page. One note is about the case study- I didn't like the format and thought it was difficult to process. Mina and Brandy asked me a while ago which case study I preferred over Slack DM and I remembered the one I chose in that conversation was much better than this one on My Amazon Guy. I like it to be data driven but not a sea of text (more visually appealing). Case studies are very important to me so this stuck out as a negative. | Overall, the copy and website seems very generic and doesn't highlight any USP. The button "get started" also seems like a weak call to action as opposed to the "Grow your Amazon Sales" & "Fast Quote" from MAG. The case studies were at the very bottom and easy to miss. All of the things in the category of what I liked from MAG is missing on this site. | "Apply for an audit" was small and not directly at the top of the page / easy to find. This may be minor but the heading text was difficult to read, on an otherwise great looking homepage | I liked it a lot. I didn't expect this site to not be an "Amazon agency" so it took me a moment to realize but overall I think it's a top notch website | Of the companies listed here, I was already familiar with Quartile as a big name in the industry since they sponsor many events but I didn't find their website or customer journey effective. Maybe in comparison to the others, but I felt it was bare, the text wasn't as easy to read, and they didn't highlight any USP that attracted my attention. I also don't think that "Request a demo" is a strong CTA since it feels vague Is there anything that makes you you hesitant when filling out the form? | No. All forms were simple and easy to fill out | The form itself was easy and straightforward. The ability to book a call right away without waiting was also nice. There was no free audit offered which is a minus. | Nothing. The form was easy to find (via large free marketing plan button) and it was easy to book a next day call | The form referred to being able to schedule a call but I didn't see the option after I added my info. documents.name: The Trivium Playbook + HR.docx
documents.content: Overview The Playbook functions as your primary reference, offering clear guidance and navigation to the exact Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) you require. Whether it's a detailed process description or a specific task protocol, the Playbook streamlines access to vital SOPs, ensuring efficient and consistent operations. If you can't find an SOP you believe should be included, we welcome your input. Please reach out to the Operations Team for assistance. Table of Contents General Notion Notion is the software Trivium uses for creating and managing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Here’s the SOP on How to: Login to Notion using Shared Access. Google Workspace Applications Drive Google Drive is a cloud-based file storage and synchronization service. It allows our team to organize files, documents, and folders efficiently. Department Shared Drives A shared drive is an organizational structure within Google Drive that lives parallel to My Drive. Shared drives support files owned by an organization rather than an individual user. Our agency utilizes department-specific shared drives to centralize and manage team resources efficiently. Access restriction measures are implemented to guarantee the privacy and security of data. Reach out to your Supervisor and/or Manager for access to your department’s shared drives. Access/Sharing Sharing files and folders is crucial for collaboration. This section will explain how to control access to documents, both internally and externally. It covers the process of setting file permissions, sharing files via links, and utilizing shared drives for streamlined collaboration. Calendar Creating an Event (Meeting) Accept/Decline It is of utmost importance to effectively handle meeting invitations and your availability. Please make sure to either accept or decline all calendar invites promptly. When you join your respective teams, you will be included in certain events at both the company and team levels. It is crucial that you review your calendar daily and accept or decline these events based on your availability. Teammate’s Calendar Understanding a teammate's schedule is essential for collaborative work. This video will show you how to view and interact with a teammate's calendar, ensuring easy coordination and scheduling of meetings or tasks. Trivium - Employees and Clients Calendar This is a comprehensive and centralized calendar which serves as a vital resource for keeping our team organized and well-informed, and ensuring that we maintain an organized and efficient work environment. This video will show you how to add this to your calendar. Calendar ID: c_ope85o1gd9tkmhauhr38r1j2do@group.calendar.google.com It includes several key events and dates, such as: Approved PTOs: This calendar displays all approved Paid Time Off (PTO) requests submitted by our employees. It allows us to track who is on leave, when, and for how long, ensuring seamless workflow planning and coverage. Employee Birthdays: Employee birthdays are a special part of our workplace culture. The calendar features the birthdates of our team members, so we can celebrate and show appreciation on their special days. National Holidays: National holidays are essential days off for our employees. This calendar marks these dates to help everyone plan around these public holidays. Client Start Dates: For our clients and projects, we include the start dates in this calendar. This information is vital for our project management and client communication, ensuring a smooth and well-coordinated kickoff for every client engagement. Meetings (Internal) Internal Meetings are meant to be an effective place for team members to use their problem-solving skills and critical thinking skills to solve any ongoing challenges. These meetings are meant to make us proactive in solving any issues client accounts or departments are facing. Team members should be ready to prepare potential solutions to overcome these obstacles. ALL team members are encouraged to share their perspectives. Call Recording Recording all calls is optional but is highly recommended, whether they are internal client calls, external client calls, or departmental calls. You may choose to record the Zoom call to your computer or to the cloud. Cameras Numerous advantages come with keeping your camera on during meetings! Encourages interpersonal connections among participants It's quite straightforward: there's value in having a virtual face-to-face conversation with the individuals you're meeting with. While many of us may wish for in-person collaboration with our colleagues in a traditional office setting, utilizing tools like Google Meet is the next best option. As humans, we have an inherent need to connect with one another. Leaving your camera on signals your interest, engagement, and attentiveness during the call. Conversely, having your camera off in virtual meetings often indicates a sense of disconnection. Sparks active involvement and engagement Seeing every team member makes it easier to engage them, solicit their input, or field questions. Maintaining your camera can also help you stay focused on meeting objectives, particularly if you tend to multitask. Conveys non-verbal cues Gestures like nodding and smiling play a significant role in gauging your team's sentiments about an upcoming project. According to Forbes, many influential leaders acknowledge that non-verbal cues, including body language, constitute 55% of all communication. Humans rely on body language to establish connections with one another. Building trust among peers requires them to feel comfortable around you. Leaving your camera on allows your personality to shine through, enabling you to leverage non-verbal cues to your advantage. Feel free to leave your camera off if: You're not feeling well There are days when working effectively means staying in your pajamas on the couch, and that's perfectly acceptable! You're in a distracting environment We've all experienced chaotic days. If your home workspace presents a backdrop of dirty dishes, children's toys, and laundry, it's advisable to keep your camera off. Balancing the need to appear professional, share your home environment with your team, and maintain a tidy background can be challenging. Nevertheless, resist the temptation to keep your home entirely devoid of the presence of children, pets, or partners—your team values seeing the real you! Virtual Meeting Etiquette Mute Yourself Remember to keep yourself muted unless you are actively speaking. Regardless of whether you're in a home or office setting, unexpected occurrences can draw attention to your square for the wrong reasons. We strive to maintain efficient meeting flow, so kindly remain on mute unless you wish to contribute, are prompted with a question, or the floor is open for discussion. This practice will also help minimize background noise during the call. Hands Up When you have a question during a Zoom meeting, make use of the hand-raise feature! Located at the bottom of your screen, you'll find an icon representing a raised hand, which will alert the host. Employ this feature judiciously! The raised hand will be clearly visible on the video frame of the participant who initiates it. It's easy to spot, but please ensure a smooth transition to your question, and if you're already speaking, wrap up your point before asking. Control The Meeting Strive to avoid speaking over other people especially your clients, yet maintain control of the call using our meeting agenda! This is a simple principle. Always keep in mind to be courteous, while also valuing your time and establishing clear expectations regarding the allotted duration for the call from the outset. documents.name: Reviews Sales Call Script v2.docx
documents.content: Reviews Sales Script. Aug 30, 2024 Purpose of this document Provide the Head of Reviews some guidelines to manage Sales Call, especially when the Sales team does not participate. Call Structure Build Rapport Hey is this [CLIENT NAME]? Hey - It’s [your name] - How is your day going so far? Awesome - [share something about your day] Remind me, what part of the world are you calling in from? Oh cool! I am from [your location] Great well - I know we got a limited amount of time here so… are you ready to jump in? Set the agenda So what I’ve found that works best on these calls is to first get a better understanding of your product, understand how many units you sell, and what the current state and the future state look like in terms of reviews. Then I can walk you through how our process works and clear up doubts. Sounds good? Product, Current State & Desired Future State So, I would love to know more about your product. Can you tell me more about it? Hints: Target customer characteristics: Who is buying your product? Mention anything relevant: age, gender, country, interests, status, profession, clues/commonalities, other characteristics. Where do your customers hang out? The success of this strategy is very much dependant on how well we target your customer. Where they may hang out? What pages do they follow? What are they interested in? Who do they follow? When customers start noticing the effects of your product? Is there an optimal time for review requesting. How much time after receiving the product is the best to ask the review after? How many units are you currently selling? That’s great, I have a much better understanding now. And what’s your goal in terms of reviews? What do you want to achieve? “Get your rating from X status to X new status within X period of time”... or “Get X number of reviews within X period of time”. Pitch our service Well [Name] - based on what you told me previously, we can definitely help… I would love to walk you through what we can offer you, how does it sound? [Walk them through the sales deck] When you reach the end of the Sales Deck, clear up questions, check client’s temperature and agree on next steps, aiming to close a start date.

documents.name: Reviews. Big Goal W_C Aug 28 2024.docx
documents.content: Reviews. Big Goal W/C Aug 28 2024 Presales Call Prep Template Goal “Create a presales call prep template with the Head of Reviews to evaluate the product but also to have selling points, so that the HoR is prepared on sales calls.” Proposed Solution The Head of Reviews will use the new Reviews Sales Script we created, to improve the quality of the Sales call, as well as to bring consistency and ensure we are covering all key points during this meeting. The recommendation is to maximize the support from the Sales team, as they should be experts in commercially positioning our services, while the HoR can support with her domain knowledge. The Head of Reviews will start filling in a Leads Database we created in the Reviews Health Database. This table includes all the information we need to prepare the Sales Call and details we need to gather on the call. This solution should be temporary and adjusted in accordance with the new HubSpot strategy and ways of working. Until then, it will help the HoR manage the leads and ensure we are consistently gathering, storing, and utilizing key information from early stages. Sales Call Template & 1-Pager Review Process Goals “To have a sales call template for Carolina, so her call structure allows for better close rates.” “Have a one-pager that explains our new process and sells this service to clients (edited by Pedro to match company standards)” Proposed Solution The Head of Reviews will use this new Sales Deck we updated and improved. We cover: Why the client should invest in the Reviews services. Why they should be partnering up with us to get this service. What’s our process and the expected timeline to see results. Case studies (to be selected based on the lead’s category) and closing. The Sales Deck includes a client-facing 1-pager that illustrates our process, the path to getting the number of reviews and rating clients are aiming for. 1 pager is also available separately here. We might want to explore including information about Quality Control in for all our services’ sales or onboarding decks. Specifically, instead of just saying “you’ll get a high quality service”, we briefly share how we assure a high quality service. We will put this on hold until we get more feedback from the Head of Sales, as she is the owner of Sales Calls. Head of Reviews thinks it would be useful to ask leads to fill out a form before the Sales Call. Director of Operations recommends gathering all necessary information on the Sales or Onboarding calls, since clients do not like filling out forms, it is less time-consuming for them if Trivium is good at gathering what we need to operate, and the chances of having a bottleneck increase by adding another step. Again, we will put this on hold until we get more feedback from the Head of Sales, as she is the owner of the Sales Process. Onboarding Call Template Goal “Have an onboarding call template that gets the maximum value making our onboarding 1 day (access to IG, boosting the post, getting money in the dedicated paypal, etc).” Proposed Solution The Head of Reviews will use this new Onboarding Deck we created. We cover: Onboarding timeline Onboarding day-by-day –this is the time we make sure we are getting what we need from the client on the call! 90-day roadmap Communication Questions Weekly reports Referral Program We cover why the client should invest in the Reviews services, why they should be partnering up with us, our process, case studies (to be selected based on the lead’s category) and closing. The slide called Weekly Reports. Example will be updated once deliverables are approved. Goals & Known Challenges will remain as an optional slide for now, as per request of the Head of Reviews to avoid potential duplication of work, as this information will be formalized prior to the contract sign-off. Reviews Day By Day Onboarding 1-Pager also available here. ClickUp Onboarding Checklist Goal “Create a comprehensive onboarding checklist in ClickUp that the team will use moving forward to ensure a streamlined and efficient onboarding.” Proposed Solution We created a Reviews workspace in ClickUp, along with this Onboarding Checklist, which should be copied whenever a new onboarding starts. Client Visual Charts Goal “Go into the existing client databases for reviews and create a visual chart that makes digesting progress so much easier and better for clients (no more than 2 charts).” Proposed Solution We duplicated the Paradise Naturals Reviews Database to showcase the charts we propose to include in the weekly report and will always be available for the customer in their database – this spreadsheet is NOT currently shared with Paradise Naturals yet. There are 2 options proposed for review: Performance Tracker – Opt. 1: Puts focus on the last 5 weeks, while including a chart to understand the performance of these 5 weeks, comparing it to our historical, all time, performance. Performance Tracker – Opt. 2: Shows all time performance since we are providing Reviews services to the client, while including a chart to understand the performance of these 5 weeks, comparing it to our historical, all time, performance. Option 1 is recommended, customers may value more knowing how Trivium is doing in a more recent period of time, and also like to have a reference to measure if the latest numbers are good or not compared to the level of performance they have received since they hired Trivium. The next recommended metric to implement is the payment/refund to review conversion rate. What’s the % of refunds that turn into positive reviews? It was also explored how to get directly from Amazon the following information about the brands over time: # Reviews Star Rating # Orders # Returns $ Sales Using Voice of the Customer and Helium10 was considered: However, this requires more effort and it was prioritized to have an MVP. Here you can find a video of the blocker we faced when trying to use Helium10. It might the case that the extension does not register new reviews daily, thus the review count jumps up once a week or so. So it may be that that part of the extension only updates once a week Proposed Next Steps Get Mina’s and Daniel’s approval of all the deliverables presented in this report. Get feedback from the new Head of Sales to continue working on these improvements in line with the strategy she starts to build for her department. Update SOPs and Process Maps when deliverables are approved. Launch the deliverables for a small group of clients/leads or all of them at once. No significant risks have been identified to prevent a big bang GoLive. Main change for the Reviews is using ClickUp. Incorporate in the contract sign off process clear information in terms of: The goals we are building our strategy upon. The expected timeline of results, especially to formalize expectations when it comes to products that require a longer testing period. Actions to be taken by the client to initiate the onboarding process, especially if they need to make any deposits or create a PayPal account. Monitor process performance. Decommission Leads Database once everything is centralized in HubSpot to keep a single and efficient source of truth. Identify opportunities of improvement for the Onboarding Checklist, setting up metrics to better understand onboarding performance as well as automations where possible. Ensure there is a backup available to backfill the Head of Reviews when she is on leave, as there are a lot of key sales and onboarding activities that are dependent on her and this could result in a bottleneck or showstopper.

documents.name: A GUIDE TO AMAZON PPC Campaign Setup.pdf
documents.content: A G U I D E TO A M A ZO N P P C Campaign Setup A successful Amazon marketing strategy starts with a PPC campaign blueprint. Optimal ad performance is achieved by having well planned, consistent campaign structures and nomenclature and if set up correctly, allows you to execute a more precise approach to optimization and reporting. GOALS OF AN AMAZON PPC STRATEGY Generate Sales Increase ad discovery and visibility boosts sales Improve Organic Rank Driving sales velocity with relevant, top of search keywords Generate Data Discovery of new profitable search terms for launching campaigns and listing optimization The Amazon advertising console is arranged according to hierarchical levels. Having a consistent and systematic approach to structuring and naming these levels facilitates effective optimization to save you time and ultimately save on wasted ad spend. Portfolio 1 Parent Product Campaign 1 Ad Group Ad Group Max 5 keywords PORTFOLIOS As well as being an effective organizational tool, portfolios are a valuable way to effectively monitor and report product performance. As each parent product is promoted by multiple campaigns, keeping one portfolio per parent product makes workflow easier to manage and provides valuable insight and control over campaigns CAMPAIGNS Separating both auto and manual campaigns based on match type outputs a higher grade of data and provides better control over campaign performance. With campaign budget distribution up to Amazon’s discretion, we see that those campaigns containing more than one match type have an uneven distribution of budget with some match types receiving more of the budget than others. Additionally, by separating each match type you are able to monitor and scale more effectively at both the budget and the bid level, as well as simplifying data monitoring and analysis. AD GROUPS Limiting each campaign to only one ad group allows you to improve both scaling and optimization efficiency as 100% of the budget is focused solely on that ad group. Confining campaigns to one ad group and one match type is the best solution for gaining control over budget distribution and scaling for profitability. NOTE: test with all campaign and match types to harvest new profitable keywords and increase sales volume KEYWORDS Unequal distribution of sessions and spend can occur when ad groups are subject to keyword dumping as the number of keywords within an ad group dramatically impacts the performance of the campaign. Campaigns achieve optimal output when keywords/product targets are limited to a maximum of 5 per ad group. For example, an ad group with 15- 20 keywords results in the top 5 generating 80-100% of the sales. Also, segregating high search volume and low search volume keywords will see that each keyword gets the opportunity to perform. When keywords of varying search volume are grouped together, the spend goes to the higher converting keyword, leaving keywords that could convert, with low or no impressions. Below is a summary outlining our most successful strategy for Amazon Sponsored Product Advertising. documents.name: Copy of Sales Cadence Template - HubSpot & Aircall.docx
documents.content: Keep scrolling to templates ↓↓↓ Template Hi {first_name}, Line 1: [Personalize the first line, if possible, with specific content or event name that your prospect interacted with, or something timely like congratulating your prospect on a recent promotion etc.] Line 2: [Ask pertaining to product/service] Line 3: [Main value proposition of your product or service goes here along with the benefit(s) it provides] Line 4: [Direct request] Closing and signature Example Hi Sarah, I saw you attended our recent webinar on how to supercharge your customer support tech stack. What did you think of it? One point in the webinar that stood out to me was that 80% of sales voicemails are not responded to by prospects. By integrating with your CRM, Aircall ensures all calls & data are automatically logged - this slashes the time spent on manual work by up to 90 seconds. Would something like this be an improvement on how your team is working at present? I'd love to touch base with you on a quick call to discuss. Best, - Jennifer Template Hi {first_name}, Line 1: [Recall to previous communication attempts] Line 2: [Ask pertaining to product/service + main value proposition of your product or service goes here along with the benefit(s) it provides] Line 3: [Direct request] Closing and signature Example Hi Alan, I wasn't able to reach out over the past few days. As HubSpot’s Service Hub Manager, I thought you would be best to speak with about your phone system, and how Aircall could be a good fit to turbocharge your support team rep’s productivity. Would you have any time this week to discuss this? Best, -Melissa Template Hi {first_name}, Line 1: [Request if it’s the right person to speak to on specific product/service] Line 2: [Detail any background research you’ve done] Line 3: [Direct request] Closing and signature Example Hi Bridget, Would you be the person in charge of the data sync capabilities for Aircall? From doing some research it seemed like you were the best person to speak to about this. If not, could you point me in the right direction? -Tim Template Hi {first_name}, Line 1: [Recall to multiple previous communication attempts] Line 2: [Offer to remove them from outreach communication] Line 3: [Direct request] Closing and signature Example Hi David, Is now a bad time to reach out? I'd be more than happy to make a note and reach out when the time is a bit better, or just let me know if you’re not the person to talk to about HubSpot and Aircall. I can remove you from my outreach with that info! Also, if you aren't responsible for the partnership opportunities at HubSpot, would you be able to point me in the right direction? Warmly, Ryan Template [This touchpoint works best with personalization. Try to find a point of relevance on your prospects profile, provide value or reiterate the personalization from Email Template #1 in the connection note.] Hey {first_name}, Line 1: [Detail why you’d like to connect on LinkedIn] Line 2: [Main value proposition of your product or service goes here along with the benefit(s) it provides + Direct request] Line 3: Closing and signature Example Hey Zoey, Given your experience, I wanted to connect on LinkedIn! I sent you a message yesterday because I noticed you attended our webinar on CS tech stack and wanted to connect to get your feedback and learn more about Aircall name. Talk soon! Ingrid Template [Tip: We’ve seen great response rates inserting a quick, customized video in LinkedIn messages to the prospect. This does take more time, so prioritize accordingly!] Hey {first_name}, Line 1: [Recall to multiple previous communication attempts + focus on their goals] Line 2: [Direct request] Line 3: Closing and signature Example Hey Lance, I shot you over a couple of emails and would love to learn more about your priorities for next year? When would you be available for a quick chat? Warmly, Nick

documents.name: HubSpot Clean Up & Reset.docx
documents.content: HubSpot Clean Up & Reset Purpose & Principles Goal: Run HubSpot as the single pane of glass from first touch → sale → billing → delivery → renewals/upsells → churn, with ChargeOver as billing source of truth and ClickUp for delivery. Principles One Company per client logo. Contacts are people; Deals are revenue events; Line Items are what was sold. Use two pipelines only: New Business (first contract) and Renewals (renewals, upsells, one‑time add‑ons). No audit pipeline. Don’t move lifecycle stages backward. Use Customer Status (Active / Paused / Churned) on Company. ChargeOver holds subscriptions, invoices, payments. HubSpot mirrors status and MRR. Tasks drive accountability (Setters, Closers, Auditor). Tickets off (delivery lives in ClickUp). Data Model (Objects & Relationships) Contacts ↔ Companies (many-to-one). Every Contact must be associated to a Company. Deals ↔ Companies (many-to-one) and ↔ Contacts (primary buyer + stakeholders). Each Deal has Line Items (Products) for what was sold. Tasks attach to Contacts and/or Deals (Setter/Closer/Auditor workload). ChargeOver syncs to Companies/Deals (MRR, subscription status, balance, LTV). ClickUp receives a project/task when Deal is Closed Won (delivery). A URL back to ClickUp is stored on the Deal/Company. Pipelines & Stages New Business (first contract) Stages (edit names to match your style; keep 6–8 max): New / Intake (10%) – Deal created (manual or from booking). Entry req: Primary Company & Contact assigned; Lead Source; Estimated Service. Discovery Scheduled (20%) – Meeting on calendar. Automation: task reminder 24h before; create “Audit Task” if Audit Required = Yes. Discovery Complete (35%) – Notes logged; budget/timeline captured. Required fields prompt: Budget known?, Decision Maker. Qualified (50%) – Fit confirmed. Automation: generate proposal task for Closer. Proposal / Scope Sent (65%) – Quote/SoW sent. Required: Line Items added. Contract Sent (80%) – Commercials agreed; contract out for signature. Verbal Commit (90%) – Pending signature/payment. Closed Won / Closed Lost – Lost reason & competitor required. Renewals (renewals, upsells, one‑time add‑ons) Stages: Identified / Scoping (20%) – Renewal or upsell opportunity created (can be auto 90 days before end date). Proposal Sent (50%) – Scope/pricing out; Line Items updated. Approved / Contract Sent (75%) – Commercial OK; contract pending. Closed Won – Triggers ChargeOver update and ClickUp work (if needed). Churned/Cancelled stage: Required fields: End Date, Churn Reason. Workflow: If Company still has ≥1 active subscription → leave Company Status = Active. If no active subs → set Company Status = Churned, stamp Churn Date, set MRR = 0. Rules New logo? First contract goes in New Business only. Any subsequent revenue (renewal terms, new services, one‑time projects) goes in Renewals. A discount or billing artifact in ChargeOver does not create another Deal. Reflect discounts via Line Items or properties. Role Playbook (Who Does What) Appointment Setter Works Contacts & early Deals. Runs first call where applicable. Books/rebooks Closer. Owns Lead Status on Contacts (New → Attempted → Connected → Qualified → Disqualified). Creates Deals (or Deals auto‑created via booking) and keeps them moving until Closer takes lead. Creates/updates Tasks; logs activity. Auditor Works from auto‑created Audit Tasks on Deals where Audit Required = Yes. Uploads result (URL) and sets Audit Completed = Yes (workflow can do this on task completion). Closer Owns active sales cycle. Advances stages, sends proposals/contracts, closes Won/Lost. CS/Delivery (in ClickUp) Triggered on Closed Won. Executes onboarding & delivery. Keeps status visible via ClickUp link on Company/Deal. Finance (ChargeOver) Receives Closed Won (Deal + Line Items) → creates/updates subscription/invoice. Syncs MRR, status, balance back to HubSpot. Operations Owns property catalog, pipelines, workflows, reports, product catalog, and data hygiene. Essential Properties (create if missing) Company (Account) Lifecycle Stage (HubSpot default) – becomes Customer on first Closed Won. Customer Status (single select): Active, Churned, Terminated. Churn Notification Date (date). Churn Reason (single select): Price, Performance, Strategy change, Brought in‑house, Payment failure, Acquisition/M&A, Other. MRR (Current) (currency) – synced from ChargeOver. LTV (Closed Won Sum) (calculated or ChargeOver sync). Billing Status (single select): Current, Past Due, In Collections. (from ChargeOver) Primary ClickUp URL (text) – project/workspace link. Active Services Count (calculated from ChargeOver) → if >0, Company Status = Active. Churn Date = populated when Active Services Count = 0. Contact Lead Status (single select): New, Attempted, Connected, Qualified, Disqualified. Role (single select): Decision Maker, Champion, User, Billing, Other. Meeting Preference / Timezone (optional). Deal (both pipelines) Deal Type (single select): New Business, Renewal, Upsell, One‑time Add‑on. Audit Required (Y/N) – conditional. Audit Completed (Y/N) – set by workflow. Audit Notes URL (text) – deliverable or doc link. Service Term Start / End (date) – if applicable. MRR (Net) (currency) – reflect net including discounts. Primary ClickUp URL (text) – created on Won. Primary Contact (HubSpot default) – must be set. Line Items (Products) Standardized catalog with clear names, SKUs, billing frequency: PPC Management (Monthly Retainer) DSP Management (Monthly Retainer) Creative Optimization (One‑time) Strategy Workshop (One‑time) Discount (Monthly) – negative line item Discount (One‑time) – negative line item Task Task Type: Call, Email, To‑do Queue: Setter – Prospecting; Setter – Follow‑ups; Auditor – Audits; Closer – Active Deals Naming convention: [Role] – [Action] – [Company] – [Deal] (e.g., Setter – Follow up proposal – Acme – NB-1234). Automations (Workflows) Contact → Deal Creation (Warm lead) Trigger: Form submit OR meeting booked via sales link with intent. Actions: Create Deal in New Business; set Owner = Setter; associate Company/Contact; set Stage = Discovery Scheduled. Audit Orchestration Trigger: Deal where Audit Required = Yes. Actions: Create Task for Auditor (due in 3 business days); add to Auditor – Audits queue; when Task completed → set Audit Completed = Yes. Proposal Guardrails Trigger: Deal moves to Proposal / Scope Sent. Actions: Require Line Items; create follow‑up task for Closer in 3 days; send Slack/Email nudge if overdue. Closed Won → Finance & Delivery Trigger: Deal = Closed Won. Actions: Send Deal + Line Items to ChargeOver (create subscription/invoice); write returned Subscription ID to Deal; set Company Customer Status = Active; create ClickUp project; save ClickUp URL on Deal & Company; create internal checklist task for onboarding. ChargeOver → Company Status Trigger: ChargeOver subscription status change. Actions: Update Company Customer Status and MRR; if total active subs = 0 → set Status = Churned and stamp Churn Date. Renewal Seeding Trigger: 90 days before Service Term End (or subscription end from ChargeOver). Actions: Create Renewals Deal with appropriate Line Items; set Owner = CSM/Closer; task to schedule renewal call. Churned / Cancelled Trigger: Renewal Deal moved to Churned stage. Actions: Set Company Customer Status = Churned; set Churn Date; capture Churn Reason; set Company MRR = 0 if no other active subs. If a single Deal is churned but Company has other active Deals/subscriptions → only reduce MRR, do not change Company Status. If final Deal is churned (Active Services Count = 0) → set Company to Churned, record Churn Date, trigger Offboarding checklist in ClickUp. Trigger: Deal = Churned. Actions: ChargeOver subscription cancelled. ClickUp task/project created with offboarding checklist (remove access, notify teams, update documentation). Update Company MRR. documents.name: Copy of Client Template for Messages (Make a copy).docx
documents.content: ClientName Reviews Messages Change everything that is marked in red - Message flow: (send a nice product picture or link to an IG post about the product) Hey Name! My name is X, I work at company name. We are doing a small giveaway for our Product Name in exchange for user feedback. I’d love to give you the product for free in exchange for simple feedback on how you like it. A line about your product. Short information. Would you be interested? (prospect replies) Thank you! 🤩 We’re doing this giveaway to receive some positive feedback. Quick question before starting- do you have an US amazon account? (prospect replies) Great! Here is how it works. Search "KeyWord" on Amazon. Tell me the total (before you buy it). Send me your Paypal. I'll send you the money. Then buy it and send me confirmation. Look up (Brand name + product) on Amazon - you should find it easily. (Prospect say yes) Awesome! The reason we do this giveaway is to get some feedback/reviews so we know how to improve our products. So excited for you to try it and get your feedback. Thanks again. This really helps. (send them screenshot of reimbursement) Here’s your payment confirmation, should arrive in a few minutes. Oh, btw, we'd be happy to gift it to 20 of your followers/friends as well. If you´re interested, just have them DM us “YourName Gift” and we will send them a free product exactly the same way! 😊 Let's spread some love!❤️ You´re the best, Name! (if the customer is hesitant to order) I totally understand your hesitation. How about we first send you the payment, and then you order? Would that make you more comfortable? (prospect say yes) Perfect! Please follow the above instructions and let me know your total before buying. (if they say later) Awesome! Let me know when you're ready! I'll be here to get your immediate reimbursement (then kindly follow up regularly, do not just wait for them to answer) Review request: Hey Name, Happy Monday. Did you get the chance to try our product name? (prospect says yes) Great! Could you please share your feedback in a quick Review on Amazon? It would mean the world to us Here’s a link so you can find it fast: amazon.com/ryp (they answers yes) You're the best! Please shoot us a screenshot of your review or under what username it will show up - for our records! Thanks a lot! (after they confirmed the review) BTW, your “Name gift” is still valid for 10 more days For people reaching out with gift code: Hi Name, Congrats - you're one of our giveaway winners!🤩 So excited for you to try our new ProductName on us -a short description about it. Quick question before starting - do you have an US Amazon account? (then follow same ordering steps) Followup messages: Hi Name, We have only 3 more samples to give away - are you still down for a free try? Hey Name, Love your recent post about xxx - you look stunning! 😍 Was wondering if you´re still interested in giving a free try to our ProductName - we have only 3 more to give away! Hey Name, Following up on this:) Hey, Name! Did you have the chance to drop a quick review for us on Amazon? ⭐ Other useful messages: (if they ask to send the product to their address) This is a giveaway on Amazon, so you can have the chance to share your feedback with other buyers there 🤩

documents.name: How To_ Log Call Notes in Hubspot.docx
documents.content: Objective The objective of this SOP is to streamline the process of transferring call summaries from HubSpot to Slack by utilizing the automation built for this purpose. Key Steps Log Meetings in HubSpot: Go to the meetings tab in the contact record. Click on "Log Meeting" and select the outcome (e.g., completed) and the type of meeting (e.g., discovery call or strategy call). Document Meeting Notes: Document your notes using snippets, selecting "closer notes". Click on "Log Activity" to automatically forward the notes to the Trivium Sales Slack channel. Review Slack Notification: Check the Slack channel for the transferred call summary. Verify that the type of call and contact information are accurately displayed. Access Notes in HubSpot: Find the same notes in the "Notes" tab in HubSpot for easy reference. Cautionary Notes Ensure that call summaries are logged as meetings in HubSpot to trigger the automation. Double-check the accuracy of the transferred information in the Slack channel. Follow the standard procedure of documenting meeting notes using snippets. Tips for Efficiency Utilize the automation to save time and effort in transferring call summaries. Consistently log meetings as per the new process to maintain data consistency. Familiarize yourself with finding and referencing notes in both the Meetings and Notes tabs in HubSpot for quick access. By following these steps and guidelines, the process of transferring call summaries from HubSpot to Slack will be efficient and accurate. If there are any questions or issues, please reach out for clarification. Link to Loom https://www.loom.com/share/a516bd4f1d804dbfbe27bb03e035e9cd

documents.name: How to determine your sale price on Amazon.pdf
documents.content: A N A M A Z O N A D V E R T I S I N G S T R AT E G Y T O P R E PA R E F O R Q 4 Create a Solid PPC Strategy Ahead of Time In the annual cycle of an Amazon seller, Q4 can be the most lucrative time of the year. With the Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales, backed up by the busy Christmas shopping period and closely followed by the new year splurges, shoppers are out in full force with their wallets ready. With increased competition and more sellers willing to increase their ad spend during the peak season, it is vital to have a solid PPC strategy in play ahead of the holiday season. When planning a strategy, look at your metrics and define your objectives. Determine where you want to improve and what changes you need to implement in order to meet those objectives. Benchmarking data history, prior to implementing changes, will allow you to monitor your progression. A 3 Step Approach for Sales and Profitability in Q4 As the holiday season approaches, ad costs start to significantly increase at the end of Q3 and do not return to normal until after the new year period. To effectively balance out the higher CPC with the increased sales volume, ranking organically is more beneficial than ever to remain profitable during the peak period. Entering Q4 with a high organic rank, for your top performing keywords, will see you come out the other side with an increase in revenue and more importantly, profitability. STEP 1: Aggressively Scale Campaign Budget & Bids to improve Organic Rank Bidding aggressively will allow you to improve your organic rank and drive free traffic, when the holiday season begins. 45 days prior to the launch of Black Friday, set a high campaign budget and bid aggressively on your top performing keywords. Pay close attention to your sessions. If your tactics are working you should see an increase in sessions, closely related to your increase in ad spend. Be prepared to not be profitable during the lead up to Q4. · High Campaign Budget · High Bid · Boost Organic Rank STEP 2: Test Top of Search Placement With an increase in buyers and sessions, comes an increase in window shoppers. Particularly in the week leading up to Black Friday. To avoid attracting window shoppers at the top of search, optimize your ad placement well in advance. Test with bid by placement to determine if your product is a top of search purchase or if it performs best in product pages or rest of search. Knowing where your customers are purchasing will allow you to determine the optimal placement for your product ad. · Top of Search First Page? · Product Pages? · Rest of Search? STEP 3: Scale for Profitability Entering Q4 With Black Friday being the opening event to Q4, use it as a benchmark to start scaling back the high budget and keyword bids. Having achieved a high organic rank for relevant keywords, reducing the bids 1 week prior to Black Friday will see you well positioned to enter the holiday season. A high, organic position in the search results will drive increased sales without relying on the high PPC typically seen during the peak season. · Decrease Campaign Budget · Decrease Bids · Monitor Organic Rank Conclusion Q4 is the opportune time for sellers on Amazon to increase revenue. By creating and executing a solid, detailed PPC plan of attack ahead of time will see the required results achieved. Follow your plan and be prepared for the most intense shopping time of the year! documents.name: SEO SOP_ How to find relevant keywords in Magnet(2).docx
documents.content: SEO SOP: How to Find Relevant Keywords in Magnet  Updated on 10 Apr 2023 •  1 Minute to read • Contributors How to Find Relevant Keywords Using Helium 10 Magnet Who is it for? This SOP is for individuals who are searching for coincidences and areas of improvement between the content you are providing (ads, A+ content, TBD, etc.) and what people are searching for currently. Objective: This SOP will help you to add value to your account by determining what people are searching on Amazon (it can be Google or Walmart too), understanding the competition, and determining trends (by seasonality) and how they affect your products too. Instructions / Steps: 1. Log in to Helium 10. 2. Click on Tools. 3. Click on Magnet. 4. Click on Find Suggestions. 5. Input the most relevant keyword for the ASIN. 6. Click on Get Keywords 7. Sort the search volume from highest to lowest. 8. Click on Search Volume Trend and analyze which keywords have more than 100% on search volume trends. 9. Look at the Search Volume data and identify the ones that have more than 500 search volumes monthly. 10. Identify the keywords that comply with the two requirements: + 100% on Search Volume Trend + 500 on Search Volume Monthly 11. Download the report, mark or highlight the relevant keywords, and share them with your advertising team, PPC POC, or creative team to take into consideration the content you are creating (Title, BP, etc). 12. To see how the main keyword is doing at a specific time, click on the Search Volumegraph icon. 13. Sort the Search Volume by 1 year, 30 days, and 90 days to identify the seasonality it affects your products. Important Note: Make sure you are looking at all the scenes when determining insights, do not base every behavior on sales. Compare with your data from previous periods/years as well as unique situations (OOS, budget adjustment, etc). Previous Facebook SOP: Initial Campaign Setup Next SEO SOP: QA Checklist for Copywriting

documents.name: Copy of 25 Proven Sales Email Templates from HubSpot, Sandler & Breakthrough Email.docx
documents.content: 25 Proven Sales Email Templates Brought to you by: 1) “Land a Meeting with Anyone” Email That Works 9 Out of 10 Times Hi [NAME], I am writing in hopes of finding the appropriate person who handles [DEPARTMENT I.E. MEDIA]? I also wrote to [PERSON X, PERSON Y, AND PERSON Z] in that pursuit. If it makes sense to talk, let me know how your calendar looks. If you are the appropriate person to speak with, what does your calendar look like? If not, who do you recommend I talk to? Thanks, [SIGNATURE] Quickly states the purpose and clearly specifies what you want them to do Provides a final call to action Ends by giving the reader the opportunity to delegate to the appropriate person 2) “First Touch Best Practice”: Email Back Strategically Hi [NAME], I appreciate the questions! There are a couple of possible answers to your questions. I want to be sure I’m giving you accurate information. Why don’t we spend a quick [CHOSEN AMOUNT OF TIME] to make sure I’m heading in the right direction? Thanks for reaching out, [YOUR NAME] Replies to guests quickly and efficiently without relaying inaccurate information Builds trust, professionalism and rapport Respecting guests’ boundaries and time will increase the portrayal of experience and success Moving guest communication from email to the phone or a video call will help you more effectively understand their situation and discover their pain points, which is the true reason for their email You’re not “spilling the candy in the lobby” – by presenting prematurely 3) "Congrats On the New Role" Email That Got a Prospect to Ask for a Meeting Hi [PROSPECT], Just left a quick message at the office for you. I chuckled a little bit when I got an automated email this morning from your predecessor, [NAME OF PREDECESSOR] who we worked with briefly, and before him, [OTHER FORMER COWORKER NAME], who we worked with as well. First and foremost, congrats on coming into this new role! I'm sure you've got a lot going on — so this conversation might be timely or not. If you're stressed, this is my go-to :) My role here is working with businesses on how they can [PURPOSE OF COMPANY]. How has your first month kicked off so far in this regard? [YOUR NAME] References previous efforts trying to help the company and mentions his co-worker’s names Leverages a trigger event of her prospect getting a new job Relates to the prospect by suggesting that taking a new role is stressful Very lightly introduces her expertise Does NOT ask for a time on his calendar and instead asks an open-ended question designed to get a response 4) First Touch Best Practice: Unveil The Wizard Hi [PROSPECT], In your last email, you said you were hoping to get started by [SPECIFIED TIME PERIOD], but I am not sure we are going to make that timing if we don’t get a meeting on the calendar this month to discuss next steps. It doesn’t sound like you are ready to move forward just yet, should I close this opportunity, or did I read the situation wrong? [YOUR NAME] References previous efforts trying to help the company during the prospect’s proposed time period Pulls back the curtain to make the salesperson seem more human 5) “Still Interested?" Email That Closed a $100,000 Deal with a Client That Went Dark Hi [FIRST NAME], Hope all is well. I had put a reminder in to check-in with you to see how things were going with the [NAME OF CAMPAIGN] initiatives. We had discussed a potential partnership a few months ago, but hadn't been able to formalize our recommended engagement. We would love to catch up and see if there are any opportunities to engage with you and help with your [DEPARTMENT (eCommerce, marketing, etc.) ] strategy. Let me know if you have some time to reconnect this week and catch up business owner to business owner on where you see things and I can provide some ideas on where we can help. Look forward to hearing from you. [YOUR NAME] References a campaign initiative the prospect shared with him Reminds the prospect of what they discussed before Focuses on finding a way to help them, not finding out if they want to buy 6) "I Just Called You" Email That Gets an 80% Response Rate within 24 Hours Hi [FIRST NAME], Sorry I missed you on the phone today, I was calling because [ONE SENTENCE REASON FOR YOUR CALL, OR NAME OF REFERRAL/EVENT THAT INTRODUCED YOU]. In my voicemail, I mentioned that I will call you back on [DATE] at [TIME] and of course you can always reach me before then at [YOUR PHONE NUMBER]. I look forward to connecting. Cheers, [YOUR NAME] Shows the prospect that you follow through Gives the prospect the option to get back to you via email instead of calling back Let’s the prospect know when you’ll follow up again 7) Follow Up Best Practice: Craft Email Messages That Build Better Rapport Hi [FIRST NAME], Thanks for sharing more information about your project. It sounds like you will have some more questions for me about how we can solve [PROSPECT’S PROBLEM], and I need a bit more info from you to make sure we can hit your timeline, budget, and objectives for the project. I am happy to move as quickly or slowly as you need. What would you like to do next? [YOUR NAME] Mirrors and matches the way the prospect wrote the email Quick response inspires prospect to move the sale forward quickly 8) Follow Up Best Practice: Craft Email Messages That Build Better Rapport Hi [FIRST NAME], Thanks for taking the time to share a little about [COMPANY], as well as the goals and challenges you face. If you would like to learn how other companies are dealing with challenges like yours, I would be happy to schedule a call. We could also talk a bit more about your challenges and determine whether or not I might be able to offer some help. If you would like to talk some more, use the convenient link below to directly schedule a time on the calendar for us to speak. [CALENDAR LINK] Best, [YOUR NAME] Focuses on making sure you can help them instead of selling Makes it easy for them to get in touch and schedule a meeting 9) “Next Step” Email That Creates Urgency [NAME], I’m writing to follow up on our last conversation. My boss asked me for an update on your account. I told him I didn’t have one. I’m not sure what makes sense to continue the conversation. What makes sense as a next step, if any? [SIGNATURE] Creates urgency Makes a clear request for next steps People can relate to having a boss and needing to provide answers to their questions Avoids selling the person and instead gently pushes the person for input and to set up the next step 10) “Next Step” Email That Creates Urgency Hi [FIRST NAME], [REFERRAL NAME] referred me to a [PIECE OF MEDIA] on [PROSPECT TOPIC OF INTEREST], and more specifically [PROSPECT TOPIC OF EXPERTISE]. We talked about it [REFERENCE PREVIOUS ENCOUNTER], so I wanted to share it with you. [1 - 2 SENTENCES EXPLAINING THE PIECE OF MEDIA] [FIRST LEARNING] [SECOND LEARNING] [THIRD LEARNING] [INFLUENCER/ENTREPRENEUR/AUTHOR] said, “[QUOTE].” While I’m not generally interested in [PROSPECT TOPIC OF INTEREST], this [PIECE OF MEDIA] changed the way I see how [PROSPECT TOPIC OF INTEREST] works. You can [WATCH/READ/LISTEN] to the [PIECE OF MEDIA] here [LINK]. Thanks! [YOUR NAME] Starts off by mentioning the referrer name. Calls out the specific opportunity and need. Brings in external quotes. 11) “Next Step” Email That Creates Urgency Dear [PROSPECT], I noticed that during the [EDUCATIONAL RESOURCE] you didn't purchase the [CTA] product at the end. And we'd love to know why. I have no intention of trying to sell you anything, but we do want to make sure that we're hitting the mark with our customers. Any feedback you can give us would help. Were you not clear on what you were getting? Is there somewhere else in your business that you need to focus? Was it too expensive? Or is your business smooth sailing? If you respond we'll send you a [FREE CONTENT] over the phone to thank you for your time spent. Please respond to this email with your reason why you didn't pur

documents.name: SEO SOP_ How to find relevant keywords in Magnet.pdf
documents.content: SEO SOP: How to Find Relevant Keywords in Magnet  Updated on 10 Apr 2023 •  1 Minute to read • Contributors How to Find Relevant Keywords Using Helium 10 Magnet Who is it for? This SOP is for individuals who are searching for coincidences and areas of improvement between the content you are providing (ads, A+ content, TBD, etc.) and what people are searching for currently. Objective: This SOP will help you to add value to your account by determining what people are searching on Amazon (it can be Google or Walmart too), understanding the competition, and determining trends (by seasonality) and how they affect your products too. Instructions / Steps: 1. Log in to Helium 10. 2. Click on Tools. 3. Click on Magnet. 4. Click on Find Suggestions. 5. Input the most relevant keyword for the ASIN. 6. Click on Get Keywords 7. Sort the search volume from highest to lowest. 8. Click on Search Volume Trend and analyze which keywords have more than 100% on search volume trends. 9. Look at the Search Volume data and identify the ones that have more than 500 search volumes monthly. 10. Identify the keywords that comply with the two requirements: + 100% on Search Volume Trend + 500 on Search Volume Monthly 11. Download the report, mark or highlight the relevant keywords, and share them with your advertising team, PPC POC, or creative team to take into consideration the content you are creating (Title, BP, etc). 12. To see how the main keyword is doing at a specific time, click on the Search Volumegraph icon. 13. Sort the Search Volume by 1 year, 30 days, and 90 days to identify the seasonality it affects your products. Important Note: Make sure you are looking at all the scenes when determining insights, do not base every behavior on sales. Compare with your data from previous periods/years as well as unique situations (OOS, budget adjustment, etc). documents.name: SEO SOP_ How to find relevant keywords in Magnet(1).docx
documents.content: SEO SOP: How to Find Relevant Keywords in Magnet  Updated on 10 Apr 2023 •  1 Minute to read • Contributors How to Find Relevant Keywords Using Helium 10 Magnet Who is it for? This SOP is for individuals who are searching for coincidences and areas of improvement between the content you are providing (ads, A+ content, TBD, etc.) and what people are searching for currently. Objective: This SOP will help you to add value to your account by determining what people are searching on Amazon (it can be Google or Walmart too), understanding the competition, and determining trends (by seasonality) and how they affect your products too. Instructions / Steps: 1. Log in to Helium 10. 2. Click on Tools. 3. Click on Magnet. 4. Click on Find Suggestions. 5. Input the most relevant keyword for the ASIN. 6. Click on Get Keywords 7. Sort the search volume from highest to lowest. 8. Click on Search Volume Trend and analyze which keywords have more than 100% on search volume trends. 9. Look at the Search Volume data and identify the ones that have more than 500 search volumes monthly. 10. Identify the keywords that comply with the two requirements: + 100% on Search Volume Trend + 500 on Search Volume Monthly 11. Download the report, mark or highlight the relevant keywords, and share them with your advertising team, PPC POC, or creative team to take into consideration the content you are creating (Title, BP, etc). 12. To see how the main keyword is doing at a specific time, click on the Search Volumegraph icon. 13. Sort the Search Volume by 1 year, 30 days, and 90 days to identify the seasonality it affects your products. Important Note: Make sure you are looking at all the scenes when determining insights, do not base every behavior on sales. Compare with your data from previous periods/years as well as unique situations (OOS, budget adjustment, etc). Previous Facebook SOP: Initial Campaign Setup Next SEO SOP: QA Checklist for Copywriting

documents.name: 5 top strategies for a winning amazon product launch.pdf
documents.content: 5 T O P S T R AT E G I E S F O R A W I N N I N G A M A Z O N P R O D U C T L A U N C H BY: MINA ELIAS, TRIVIUM Have you ever wondered how some products on Amazon seem to take off while others struggle to gain traction? On the world’s largest ecommerce platform, where millions of sellers vie for consumers’ attention, having a great product just isn’t enough. Achieving success is about launching products to capture — and retain — customers’ interest. A successful Amazon product launch can make or break your business. To ensure a winning product launch, you need a well-planned strategy that includes research, marketing, and optimization. Here are five key product launch strategies that not only meet the needs of your target market, but also generate revenue and growth for your business. 1. Learn About Your Market A surefire way to create a lackluster launch? Not conducting marketing research. Without knowing how to meet customer needs or stand out in a crowded marketplace, businesses can launch products that result in low sales, negative reviews, or even a damaged reputation that can be difficult to recover from. By conducting thorough market research, identifying market gaps, and pinpointing potential demand before launching a product, on the other hand, you can ensure that your product fills a specific need. Analyzing fundamental aspects, such as market demand, profitability, suppliers, delivery, and target audience, plays a crucial role in validating the potential success of a product. Amazon provides several tools for market research, including the Best Sellers listings, the Movers and Shakers list, and the ability to browse Amazon storefronts. Tools like ManageByStats and D8aDriven can also help you find profitable products by analyzing metrics such as sales volume, keyword search volume, and pricing. By utilizing these tools, you can identify products with high demand and low competition and track your competitors' sales trends, pricing strategies, and marketing tactics. 2. Conduct Keyword Research Keyword research is an essential aspect of any new Amazon product launch strategy. The process enables you to identify the most relevant keywords and phrases that potential customers use when searching for products similar to yours. After you’ve found the right keywords, incorporating them into your pay-per-click (PPC) ad campaigns to improve your search ranking and increase your visibility to customers is easy with management software like PPC Entourage. The result: a big revenue boost. Amazon provides a wealth of information that sellers can use for keyword research, such as the search bar autocomplete feature and the suggested search terms that appear at the bottom of the search results page. Analyzing your competitors’ listings can also give you valuable insights into the keywords they’re targeting and the language they’re using to describe their products. You can also use third-party tools to identify keywords relevant to your products and gain insights into each keyword’s search volume and competition level. By using a combination of Amazon, competitor listings, and third-party tools, you can create a comprehensive list of targeted keywords that will help you optimize your product listings, give you maximum visibility into your products’ performance, and increase your chances of success on Amazon. 3. Optimize Your Product Listing Keywords are essential, but if they’re not connected to a compelling product listing, an Amazon product launch can fall flat. As you craft your product listing, ensure you incorporate SEO elements, engaging A+ content, and a captivating brand story. When you leverage quality research and insights into products and your competitors with SellerTools, you can make sure you’re maximizing your listing. By optimizing the product listing with relevant keywords and providing valuable information about your brand, you can enhance the visibility of your products and establish a strong online presence. Here are a few areas to pay attention to. PRODUCT IMAGES Today’s consumers expect an enhanced experience when they visit your product pages. Incorporating high-quality images and videos that showcase your product's use, features, and benefits is crucial for creating an exceptional customer experience and boosting conversion rates. By providing visual aids, you can present information in a more engaging and interactive way, allowing customers to quickly discover your product’s unique benefits and features. TITLE AND BULLET POINTS Two must-have features of your Amazon product listing: a compelling title and bullet points. Your product title should be clear, concise, and attention-grabbing. A well-crafted title accurately reflects the product and includes relevant keywords that enable customers to quickly find it in search. Bullet points should highlight the product's key features and benefits, making it easy for customers to understand what they're getting. They should be short, straightforward, and easy to read and understand. Similarly to the title, including relevant keywords in the bullet points can improve the product's visibility and help it rank higher in search results. BRAND STORY, PRODUCT DESCRIPTIONS, AND A+ CONTENT Your brand story is your opportunity to connect with potential customers on a deeper level and differentiate your product from competitors. This section should be authentic and compelling, providing insight into your brand's values, mission, and history. Use storytelling techniques to engage potential customers and create an emotional connection. A strong brand story can increase brand loyalty and create brand advocates who will spread the word about your product. The product description should be clear, concise, and engaging, providing potential customers with all the information they need to make an informed purchasing decision. Use bullet points and short paragraphs to craft an accessible description, and incorporate relevant keywords to increase search visibility. Most importantly, ensure that the product description accurately reflects the product and explains how the product can benefit a user. A+ content is an additional opportunity to showcase your product's key features and benefits by using enhanced images, videos, and additional text to provide a more immersive customer experience. Because A+ content offers a more comprehensive view of the product, it can improve conversion rates and increase customer satisfaction. Want a free audit and actionable steps on how to improve your PPC? SCAN THIS! PRICING, REVIEWS, AND FBA When launching a new product on Amazon, you need to consider pricing. To maximize your sales potential, it's essential to price your product competitively. Conduct thorough research on your competitors' prices, and adjust your pricing strategy accordingly. Customers are always looking for the best deal, so offering a lower price than your competition can give you a significant advantage. But you also need to ensure your pricing is profitable long-term. For more sustainable results, consider offering one-time or limited discounts. The real Amazon MVP? Reviews. Positive product reviews provide social proof, build trust with potential customers, and improve your product's ranking in search results. Encourage customers to leave positive reviews. Respond to any negative reviews promptly and professionally to show that you care about your customers' experiences. Remember that customer feedback is valuable and can help you identify areas for improvement. Staying on top of potential negative reviews is easier with automated notifications. AMZAlert monitors your listings around the clock to keep you up to date with any alerts about inventory, listings, or negative reviews, and more. Fast and reliable shipping is another top priority for customers, and by utilizing fulfillment by Amazon (FBA), you can beat your competitors’ shipping speed. FBA offers benefits such as Prime eligibility, which can in
