documents.content: Click File → Make a Copy for your own editable version Sales Playbook Template Company Overview Provide an overview and address the following questions: What does your company do? What is the industry and where does your company fit? Mission & values of the company. What is the long-term strategy/vision of your company? Organization Chart For the high-level one, provide a functional organizational chart with the name of representing each function, that will allow the reader to know who to look for if they need assistance. Sales Team Chart Sales team, that explains job functions, roles, and relationships. Communication Guide Optional: Guide on how your team should work with the management team. Industry This section should include the following information: Industry Overview, trends/movement within the industry Good to know industry terminologies General challenges within the industry Customer Profiles (that you focus on/target) Pain points share by those customers (for each persona) Product & Pricing Provide the the following information: Product Overview/Vision Product/Feature briefs (1 for each segment or personas) Pricing information (or how it is determined) Sales Process/Workflow Process Mapping Flowchart Inbound/Outbound Prospecting This section should include information on: List of terminologies used to describe inbound and outbound process Information on qualifying a lead Information on booking discovery/demos. Qualifying a Lead Discovery/Demos This section should include information on: What’s considered a discovery? When do you qualify someone into the discovery stage? How is it different from demos? How to properly conduct a demo? Who should be involved? Scripts to be used during the call. Proposal/Negotiations/Closing Include information on: Presentation best practices Negotiation tactics Internal case studies that won clients Pitch Decks & other resources Renewals/Reference Include information on: Guide on maintaining relationship with current customers Upsell Strategy Referral Strategies Messaging Library A great messaging library should address all messaging across all platforms: Introductory/overview emails Follow ups (for every stage) Call scripts, voice mails, Response to objections Social Media Messaging (LinkedIn, Twitter, Instagram, etc) Briefs/Snippets (product, case studies, press release, blogs) Operational Best Practices Prospect Research Guide Materials to aid in researching sales leads Here is an article you can include. documents.content: INBOUND New Lead - Audit Request Received, includes following up on Permissions Email templates Audit Completion Post-Audit Email templates Sales Call - for Closing - only section that script is needed Post-Sales Call Client Rejection or Onboarding - Strategic direction call/ PPC Team takes over OUTBOUND Prospecting Audit - do we still send the audit via email or do we schedule a Sales Call instead to discuss findings and include client discovery? Post-Audit Sales Call - is the Sales call intended for Discovery? Post-Sales Call Client Rejection or Onboarding PPC Management Procedures Overview PPC Management The PPC Management Process ● “Where are you calling in from?” ● Set the FrameWork for the call ○ “This is our strategy call. The goal of this call is to find your needs and challenges with Amazon.” ○ “Taking Notes, Not Gaming” ○ “As much as you are interviewing us, we are interviewing you. We want to make sure we fit and build a long steady partnership. Sometimes brands may not feel it's a good fit, and sometimes we don't feel it's a good fit.” ○ “We determine that by the end of the call we will know if we want to move to the next stage.” ● Introduce GPA (Growth Potential Analysis) ● “Being transparent, the GPA is great because it really takes the guesswork out of what we can do. “Shows money being left on the table.” ● “We get guest permissions into the account and take a deep dive and get some good solid data on your current PPC.” ● “It's going to really tell us where there is a lot of room for Canopy to rock it for you, or it won't. Which we will be able to tell you based on what we see when we implement our strategies.” ● Lead Analyst - Craig ● DO YOU HAVE ANY QUESTIONS?? ● “So tell high level what's currently going on with Amazon?” ● “Familiar with Brian Johnson, (GODFATHER OF AMAZON PPC). Co-Founder” ● “You remind me of….” (Story Time) ● Questions/Discovery: These are in the DealCard, and the field needs to be filled out on the call. ● Started on Amazon in: ● Brand: ● What is their Pain Point? ● Monthly PPC Sales? (CONFIRM THROUGH SELLER CENTRAL) ● Total Monthly Sales? (CONFIRM THROUGH SELLER CENTRAL) ● What is their ACoS? ● Breakeven ACoS? (Analytics team wants to know) (Target 30%) ● Who are your top 5 Competitors? ● Where do you see yourself in 6 Months and 12 Months? (“IF WE GOT COFFEE TOGETHER”) ● How is your current supply chain? Issues? Need assistance? (GEMBAH) ● Avg 30 Day Conversion Percentage (CONFIRM THROUGH SELLER CENTRAL) ● Have You Done Any Split A/B Testing? ● How well are your listings optimized?? (Scale of 1-10) ● Selling in the US and/or other marketplace? (if applicable) ● Do they have an Amazon store? (If no link available) ● 1P or 3P Seller? (Ratio) ● Are they Brand Registered? ● How Many SKUs do they have? ● Seller Account Name? ● Are they the owner or decision maker on the account? ● Find and target the Pain Point so Canopy can help solve their issue ● BRAND LAUNCH QUESTIONS: ● Does the product(s) already exist? ■ If so, is it already being sold through a channel other than Amazon? If so, please provide sales volume and revenue numbers. ● List the products, sizes and preliminary Amazon price points ■ If sizes and price points are still unknown, provide your best educated guess ● If you have a D2C website, provide URL ● What features and benefits are integral to your product and give you an advantage? ■ By product type ■ Include anything important, like ingredients, materials of construction, certifications, etc ■ Target demographic, if applicable ● What Brands are your direct competitors on Amazon? ■ What specific products are most similar to your products? Include specific ASINs, if possible. ● What would YOU type into the search bar to find your product? ■ Provide 3-5 search phrases, by product, if possible ● When are you looking to go live on Amazon? ● Get the FLYWHEEL GOING: Listing Visibility, Organic Rank, PPC Paid Rank. ● WHAT OTHER QUESTIONS CAN I ANSWER FOR YOU? ● Facts about PPC Management Service ● Minimum partner pays $1,495 Management Fee (BE TRANSPARENT, WE ARE $$$) (Customize pricing depending on scope of work) (Range: $1,495-$5k/mo) ● Set up Fee (Mirrors Management Fee) ● 5% Revenue Share (Tiers down as we grow you) ● 12 Month Contract but 90 Day out with 30 Day Notice ● NO ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, ALL HUMAN INTERACTIONS AND DECISIONS. HYBRID APPROACH. ● 2 Strategy Calls every month minimum w/ Ad Manager to discuss strategies, goals, recommendations, and Ad spend. (One Ad Manager Assigned and 6 ad specialists) (Specialist are in the account 4 out of 7 days a week) ● Weekly Account Reporting/Summaries Sent Out ● Monthly Objectives Planner with you ● SET GOALS AND KPIs ● Services with PPC Management ● Existing Campaign Audit ● Conversion-Based Bid Optimization ● Budget Review & Revision ● Keyword & Search Term Research & Optimization ● Negative Keyword Research ● Ongoing Campaign Effectiveness Assessment Permissions for GPA ● After Scheduling get user permissions ● Click on “Settings” in Seller Central ● Click “User Permissions” ● Send email address through Zoom Chat to send a invitation for permissions ● Check Tetra Doc for Partner Accounts: https://app.tettra.co/teams/canopy-management/pages/obtaining-partner-amazon-account-access-using-alias-partner-notifications-gmail-account ● Accept Email Invite ● Download Authenticator and Scan QR Code - https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1bJF8kmAObzdPwwsnidfL7euimJWPbj2X?usp=sharing ● Log Into Seller Central using ● Check Tetra Doc for Partner Accounts: https://app.tettra.co/teams/canopy-management/pages/obtaining-partner-amazon-account-access-using-alias-partner-notifications-gmail-account ● Once Logged in, Select Marketplace (if applicable) ● Have Partner Refresh Page and Click “Manage Permissions” ● Permissions - https://canopymanagement.com/onboarding/ ● Advertising > Campaign Manager > View & Edit ● Inventory > Manage Inventory/Add a Product > View & Edit ● Performance > Marketplace Appstore > View & Edit ● Reports > Business Reports, Sales Summary > View & Edit ● Reports > Product Ads Performance Reports > View ● Vendor Central Permissions Post Discovery Call Steps ● GET GPA SCHEDULED (LOOK AT CRAIG AND LEANN’S SCHEDULE) (A WEEK OUT) in Hubspot ● Schedule 30 Minutes GPA Prep 1 day before and GPA Prep 15 minutes before GPA in Hubspot (INCLUDE CRAIG AND LEANN) ● Send information in Slack to Sales Support Analysis Group ● Update Deal Card in Hubspot ● Stage ● Update Tasks ● Questions and GPA Field filled in on Deal Card ● Create Partner Folder on Shared Drive - Click Here ● Upload Zoom Recording into Google Drive Folder. ● Create a copy of PPC GPA Sales Deck Template - https://drive.google.com/drivex/folders/1MuJ7F5gVH5_46a5PrfqoLU1G3wks0O4t?usp=sharing ● Move the copy to your Partner folder and rename “CANOPY + Prospect Name - GPA” ● CREATE COPY of Full Service Pricing Calculator and move it your Partner Folder - https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Q0giCMJwYRSyH0h6BrRh7ANFYdzxUeK6?usp=sharing ● Rename it ““Partner” Pricing Calculator” ● Adjust the numbers to fit Standard PPC Management guidelines. ■ Use pricing table in the calculator to determine what their monthly flat fee should be (Enter it into the green cell for the PPC row) ■ Delete out all other rows pertaining to “other” services ■ Enter Estimated last 30 days PPC Sales into green field for Estimated PPC Sales for calculating rev share. ■ Look at pricing table to determine what % of PPC Sales we will use for calculating rev share. (ie, default is 5%) ● ***General Rule of Thumb: We do not want the total flat fee + estimated rev share to surpass 10% of their PPC sales. History shows they will leave us when our fees come up toward that 10% of PPC Sales number*** ● Update Deal Card Value in Pipedrive for reporting purposes. ● Verify Permissions are set if not done on call GPA Prep - DAY BEFORE GPA PREP MEETING ● Evaluate listings and catalog ○ Do they need LOT? documents.name: SEO SOP_ Competitor Research.pdf
documents.content: SEO SOP: Competitor Research Updated on 22 Jun 2023 • 4 Minutes to read • Contributors Competitor Research Report Using Helium10 Xray Who is this for? To individuals who seek to provide a high-level overview of how your competitors are faring on the Amazon marketplace. Objectives: To know where your listings stand in the competition; To determine the average monthly data of a specific product category, including competitor prices, search ranks, sales, reviews, average ratings, revenue, fees, and more. Sample Worksheet: Competitor Research Report - Wooden Soap Tray I. Identify which ASINs/products you need to work on In most cases, you will be provided with a set of listings to work on. But for the sake of this learning material, we will be focusing on wooden soap trays as our target listing. To look for competitors on Amazon, begin by using wooden soap trays as your main keyphrase and hit the search button. Figure 1. II. Download the listings Once the results page renders, run the listings through Helium10’s Xray (figure 2) and wait until you see the image as shown in Figure 3. Figure 2. Figure 3. Download all the listings’ data by clicking the download button (figure 4). Next, access the downloaded file and add a name to help identify which file you need to consolidate. This will be better explained on page 4. Figure 4. Figure 5. Repeat the process until you reach the 5th or 6th page. III. Consolidate Access your Google Drive and create a draft spreadsheet to consolidate all the listings from each of the downloaded H10 X-ray files. Rename the spreadsheet using this format: Name – Competitor Research Report. From here, you can now start consolidating all the listings by importing the files you downloaded. Figure 6. When importing the downloaded files, be sure to select replace data at the selected cell instead of creating a new spreadsheet, or else you will wipe out all of the existing information on your spreadsheet. Once successfully loaded, highlight the first row with any color of your choice to emphasize the headers. You may also opt to freeze the first row and make the header row’s font bold in order to make it visually appealing. Next, go to the bottom part of the worksheet, click on the cell, and import the second downloaded H10 X-ray file (figure 7). Do this until you have imported all the downloaded files. Also, you may rename the tab with the name of the listing you’re creating the competitor research on. Figure 7. Create a filter to sort the BSR data from A to Z or from smallest to largest. Then, remove listings with neither revenue nor BSR data. You will see some listings without revenue but have BSR data, please do not remove them. Likewise, if you see some listings with revenue but no BSR data, do not remove them as well. Figure 8. The next step is to move all listings without revenue data to the bottom part of the worksheet, ensuring that the first listing is the product with the lowest BSR data and followed by the next, all in ascending order. From here, you can now remove listings with duplicate BSR data. To do this, go to Data, click on data cleanup, and remove duplicates. See Figure 10. Figure 9. Figure 10. IV. Apply Conditional Formatting This part requires product knowledge; it is an advantage if you have an idea about what the product is about. Research is key. Because the product is about wooden soap trays, we can use the mentioned keywords as our format rules to retain the right competitors and remove irrelevant listings. Begin by highlighting the entire column A and click on Conditional Formatting. First, type in the keyword wood (from wooden) and apply it as the first format rule, with range A:A (figure 12). You will see several highlighted and unhighlighted cells. At this part, go over the unhighlighted listings and check if they qualify in the wood category. You can also check the keywords used on those listings. Figure 11. Most of the unhighlighted listings contain the keyword bamboo, which is classified as wood. This gives us an idea that the said keyword can be used as the second or alternate format rule. See Figure 13. From here, we can then remove those irrelevant listings (i.e. ceramic, plastic, glass, etc.) that were left unhighlighted. Additionally, we can narrow down the list of competitors by applying the next set of format rules by using the keywords soap and tray and removing all irrelevant (or unhighlighted) listings. To further remove irrelevant listings, take a look at one of the unhighlighted listings and see what keywords are used. In this case, the keywords dispenser and white were the common words used in their listings, thus we shall be using these keywords as the next format rules. Figure 12. Figure 13. Next, delete all the highlighted listings from the sheet as all the highlighted listings contain characteristics that we don’t want in our report. Do not touch the unhighlighted rows. Once you’ve used all the formatting rules possible to detect irrelevant listings, and deleted all the irrelevant listings from the sheet, you can then transfer your output to the final folder using the official template. Figure 14. As shown in Figure 14, the title on your sheet should reflect the title on your summary table. Prices, Revenue, and FBA Fees should all have a currency sign. Likewise, the data on Sales, BSR, Active Sellers, Review Count, Images, and Review Velocity should be in whole numbers. And lastly, the Creation Date data should be in date format. By applying the learnings from this document, you will demonstrate knowledge of the correct creation of competitor research reports. documents.name: Advertising Strategy to Prepare for Q4.pdf
documents.content: A N A M A Z O N A D V E R T I S I N G S T R AT E G Y T O P R E PA R E F O R Q 4 Create a Solid PPC Strategy Ahead of Time In the annual cycle of an Amazon seller, Q4 can be the most lucrative time of the year. With the Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales, backed up by the busy Christmas shopping period and closely followed by the new year splurges, shoppers are out in full force with their wallets ready. With increased competition and more sellers willing to increase their ad spend during the peak season, it is vital to have a solid PPC strategy in play ahead of the holiday season. When planning a strategy, look at your metrics and define your objectives. Determine where you want to improve and what changes you need to implement in order to meet those objectives. Benchmarking data history, prior to implementing changes, will allow you to monitor your progression. A 3 Step Approach for Sales and Profitability in Q4 As the holiday season approaches, ad costs start to significantly increase at the end of Q3 and do not return to normal until after the new year period. To effectively balance out the higher CPC with the increased sales volume, ranking organically is more beneficial than ever to remain profitable during the peak period. Entering Q4 with a high organic rank, for your top performing keywords, will see you come out the other side with an increase in revenue and more importantly, profitability. STEP 1: Aggressively Scale Campaign Budget & Bids to improve Organic Rank Bidding aggressively will allow you to improve your organic rank and drive free traffic, when the holiday season begins. 45 days prior to the launch of Black Friday, set a high campaign budget and bid aggressively on your top performing keywords. Pay close attention to your sessions. If your tactics are working you should see an increase in sessions, closely related to your increase in ad spend. Be prepared to not be profitable during the lead up to Q4. · High Campaign Budget · High Bid · Boost Organic Rank STEP 2: Test Top of Search Placement With an increase in buyers and sessions, comes an increase in window shoppers. Particularly in the week leading up to Black Friday. To avoid attracting window shoppers at the top of search, optimize your ad placement well in advance. Test with bid by placement to determine if your product is a top of search purchase or if it performs best in product pages or rest of search. Knowing where your customers are purchasing will allow you to determine the optimal placement for your product ad. · Top of Search First Page? · Product Pages? · Rest of Search? STEP 3: Scale for Profitability Entering Q4 With Black Friday being the opening event to Q4, use it as a benchmark to start scaling back the high budget and keyword bids. Having achieved a high organic rank for relevant keywords, reducing the bids 1 week prior to Black Friday will see you well positioned to enter the holiday season. A high, organic position in the search results will drive increased sales without relying on the high PPC typically seen during the peak season. · Decrease Campaign Budget · Decrease Bids · Monitor Organic Rank Conclusion Q4 is the opportune time for sellers on Amazon to increase revenue. By creating and executing a solid, detailed PPC plan of attack ahead of time will see the required results achieved. Follow your plan and be prepared for the most intense shopping time of the year! documents.name: PPC CAMPAIGN OPTIMIZATION-3.docx
documents.content: AMAZON PPC CAMPAIGN OPTIMIZATION WORKFLOW WHY YOU NEED AN OPTIMIZATION STRATEGY Optimal PPC performance requires frequent and consistent optimization. Sellers who actively and efficiently optimize their ad campaigns almost always see better results. First, consider the 2 main goals of PPC: 1. To drive traffic for the minimum cost possible 2. Improve organic rank for long-term sales with no advertising costs A well-defined optimization strategy to “fine-tune” PPC campaigns aimed at lowering the ad spend while increasing traffic has a proportional impact on organic rank and, when combined, will achieve a higher sales volume with a desirable return on ad spend (RoAS). While there are many ways to optimize PPC campaigns, we find the most effective approach is to break it down into 4 stages. By keeping to a weekly schedule of optimizing and reporting, we are able to maintain control over marketing performance and profitability. STAGE 1 BULKSHEET BID OPTIMIZATION Determine which keywords drive action and convert and which keywords are having a negative impact on campaign performance. The goal is to set keyword bids as low as possible while still maintaining results by: Building on what’s running profitably to drive more traffic and increase profitable sales. Cut back on wasted ad spend, sending budget to the more profitable keywords and effectively improving campaign performance. Amazon’s bulksheets simplifies bid optimization by enabling bid adjustments to be made across multiple campaigns all at once. Optimization step 1 – Keywords with a good ACoS If a keyword is performing below target ACoS, incrementally increase the bid in small amounts. Increases in bids will drive more traffic and increase sales velocity. Optimization step 2 – Keywords with a poor ACoS If a keyword is performing above target ACoS, incrementally decrease the bid in small amounts. Reducing bids decreases ACoS and lowers wasted ad spend. Optimization Step 3 – Non Converting Keywords If a keyword has 5 or more clicks and no sales, incrementally lower the bid. Reducing bids decreases ACoS and lowers wasted ad spend. Optimization Step 4 – Keywords with low impressions Increase bids on keywords with less than 300 impressions. A higher bid will drive traffic, improving ad visibility and CTR. STAGE 2 SEARCH TERM REPORT KEYWORD OPTIMIZATION Keywords are the building blocks of a PPC campaign. Amazon’s search term report (STR) displays the exact terms that buyers use to search for products so you can identify which search terms are profitable and which are resulting in wasted ad spend. Optimization Step 1 – Profitable Search Terms/ASINs Identify profitable search terms and ASINs from auto, broad, and phrase campaigns. Create a list of potential keywords/ASINs and launch in new campaigns (maximum of 5 keywords/ASINs per campaign). Optimization Step 2 – Non Profitable Search Terms/ASINs Identify search terms/ASINs that are getting clicks but no sales or those with an ACoS above 100%. Add as negative exact match type within the corresponding campaign in which they are performing poorly. Optimization Step 3 – Irrelevant Search Terms Identify customer search terms, for which your product is being displayed but is not relevant. Add as negative exact or negative phrase match within the corresponding campaign. STAGE 3 PLACEMENT REPORTS Placement reports provide data on the impact of ad position on exposure and conversions. Adjusting bids by placement allows sellers to monitor campaign bid performance and make specific bid adjustments to aggressively enhance visibility. Optimization Step 1 – Bid Adjustment by Placement Determine which placement is most effective at the campaign level. Increase bid adjustment for high performing, high RoAS campaigns. STAGE 4 CAMPAIGN BUDGET OPTIMIZATION Campaign budgets play a role in the effectiveness of a campaign. To make the most of traffic and customer demand, ads should be visible all day, every day. Optimization Step 1 – Campaign Budget Increase Optimize campaign budgets based on the profitability at the campaign level. Increase the budget by 100% on performing campaigns with a good RoAS.g. RoAS greater than 3. documents.name: 5 AMAZON PPC MISTAKES TO AVOID.pdf
documents.content: 5 A M A Z O N P P C M I S TA K E S T O A V O I D 1. Poor Campaign Structure Campaigns with more than 1 ad group and/or campaigns with more than 5 keywords/ASINs, spreads the budget too thin and leaves it to Amazon’s discretion to distribute the budget where it believes spend is working best. Campaigns with mixed match types limits your control over your budget, placement bid settings and makes performance analysis difficult, as each match type is driven with a different intent. S O L U T I O N 1 campaign 1 match type 1 ad group max 5 keywords/ASINs AUTO CAMPAIGNS MANUAL CAMPAIGNS Close Loose Compliments Substitutes Exact Broad Phrase Ad Group Ad Group Ad Group -Keyword A -Keyword A -Keyword A -Keyword B -Keyword B -Keyword B -Keyword C -Keyword C -Keyword C -Keyword D -Keyword D -Keyword D -Keyword E -Keyword E -Keyword E Portfolio 1 Parent Product Campaign 1 Ad Group Ad Group Max 5 keywords 2. Budget Caps Account level budget caps, portfolio budget caps or low campaign budgets affects performance. Account/Portfolio Budget Low Campaign Budget · Increasing bids may be ineffective if · Campaigns are throttled Amazon distributes budget elsewhere · Campaigns underperform · Good performing campaigns will not · Running out of budget results continue driving sales if the budget in loss for sales is exhausted S O L U T I O N Set budgets exclusively at the campaign level for tighter control. Allow campaigns to perform and control the spend by optimizing bids and negating non-profitable search terms/ASINs. 3. Listing Cannibalization A high keyword rank for both sponsored and organic ads results in unnecessary wasted ad spend as buyers will click on the first ad they see, a sponsored ad will likely receive more clicks, even if your organic listing is already positioned in front of your target audience. The same can occur when running multiple ads types such as sponsored products, sponsored brand headline and sponsored brand video. There is the potential for a high number of clicks with a negative impact on ACoS. S O L U T I O N When ranked high organically, lower bids for sponsored ads on those keywords with the high organic rank and monitor for a decrease in ad spend with little to no impact on total sales volume. If running multiple ad types and clicks and sessions are not somewhat proportional, consider limiting to the best performing. 4. Targeting all Variations When targeting all variations within the one campaign Amazon chooses where to distribute the budget and which variation receives the most impressions. The best performing variation, the one that attracts the most attention and has the highest CTR may be underperforming. S O L U T I O N Send traffic to all variations by initially targeting each variation within the same ad group. After 2-3 weeks, Use the Advertised product Report to determine which variation performs the best. Reduce wasted ad spend and apply more aggressive bidding, to drive more traffic to the best performing variation by pausing the variations with lower CTRs. Once the traffic is driven to your page, your buyer will be presented with all your variations. 5. Neglecting to Add Negative Keywords/ASINs Neglecting to add negative keywords is a costly mistake resulting in poor performing campaigns appearing for irrelevant or non-profitable customer search terms, resulting in low conversion rates and a high amount of wasted ad spend. S O L U T I O N Increase campaign profitability by regularly downloading search term reports to determine search terms/ASINs that are irrelevant/non profitable and negate in the campaign. documents.content: A N A M A Z O N A D V E R T I S I N G S T R AT E G Y T O P R E PA R E F O R Q 4 Create a Solid PPC Strategy Ahead of Time In the annual cycle of an Amazon seller, Q4 can be the most lucrative time of the year. With the Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales, backed up by the busy Christmas shopping period and closely followed by the new year splurges, shoppers are out in full force with their wallets ready. With increased competition and more sellers willing to increase their ad spend during the peak season, it is vital to have a solid PPC strategy in play ahead of the holiday season. When planning a strategy, look at your metrics and define your objectives. Determine where you want to improve and what changes you need to implement in order to meet those objectives. Benchmarking data history, prior to implementing changes, will allow you to monitor your progression. A 3 Step Approach for Sales and Profitability in Q4 As the holiday season approaches, ad costs start to significantly increase at the end of Q3 and do not return to normal until after the new year period. To effectively balance out the higher CPC with the increased sales volume, ranking organically is more beneficial than ever to remain profitable during the peak period. Entering Q4 with a high organic rank, for your top performing keywords, will see you come out the other side with an increase in revenue and more importantly, profitability. STEP 1: Aggressively Scale Campaign Budget & Bids to improve Organic Rank Bidding aggressively will allow you to improve your organic rank and drive free traffic, when the holiday season begins. 45 days prior to the launch of Black Friday, set a high campaign budget and bid aggressively on your top performing keywords. Pay close attention to your sessions. If your tactics are working you should see an increase in sessions, closely related to your increase in ad spend. Be prepared to not be profitable during the lead up to Q4. · High Campaign Budget · High Bid · Boost Organic Rank STEP 2: Test Top of Search Placement With an increase in buyers and sessions, comes an increase in window shoppers. Particularly in the week leading up to Black Friday. To avoid attracting window shoppers at the top of search, optimize your ad placement well in advance. Test with bid by placement to determine if your product is a top of search purchase or if it performs best in product pages or rest of search. Knowing where your customers are purchasing will allow you to determine the optimal placement for your product ad. · Top of Search First Page? · Product Pages? · Rest of Search? STEP 3: Scale for Profitability Entering Q4 With Black Friday being the opening event to Q4, use it as a benchmark to start scaling back the high budget and keyword bids. Having achieved a high organic rank for relevant keywords, reducing the bids 1 week prior to Black Friday will see you well positioned to enter the holiday season. A high, organic position in the search results will drive increased sales without relying on the high PPC typically seen during the peak season. · Decrease Campaign Budget · Decrease Bids · Monitor Organic Rank Conclusion Q4 is the opportune time for sellers on Amazon to increase revenue. By creating and executing a solid, detailed PPC plan of attack ahead of time will see the required results achieved. Follow your plan and be prepared for the most intense shopping time of the year! documents.name: 10 ways to beat the Amazon Algor.pdf
documents.content: 1 0 W A Y S T O B E AT T H E A M A Z O N A L G O R I T H M Amazon works with its own proprietary search algorithm to determine which products are placed at the top of search results and will always promote the products that are most likely to convert. 1. Seller Authority With the aim of providing a positive customer experience, the Amazon algorithm places importance on a seller's previous, as well as current, activity on the platform. Active Time Feedback Performance on Amazon Rating Metrics Inventory Fulfillment Size of Product Levels Method Catalogue 2. Sales History A history of consistent sales, plus sales velocity, weighs heavily on organic rank. The more sales being generated and the higher the potential for sales in the future, the higher Amazon will rank a product. 3. Impressions The more views a product receives, not only on the Amazon Marketplace, but also affiliate and partner sites, the higher Amazon will rank a product. 4. Click-Through-Rate (CTR) CTR represents both ad relevance and customer engagement. A high CTR indicates a high volume of traffic which is indexed by the algorithm to improve product rank. 5. Conversion Rate (CVR) As a measure of the rate at which potential customers view and then buy a product, CVR is a pivotal factor in a better product ranking. A higher conversion rate means more sales which contributes to a higher rank by Amazon’s algorithm. 6. Organic Sales Sales generated from organic product listings, have a powerful influence on the Amazon algorithm. Sales velocity from organic sales is prioritized over sales from paid advertising when it comes to product ranking. 7. PPC Sales PPC is a key driver for increased traffic, CTR, CVR and sales velocity. All of which are important ranking factors and contribute to a solid organic presence. 8. Internal Sales Sales generated from placements other than through search results, such as ‘frequently bought together’, ‘recommended’ or ‘similar products’ will influence product ranking. 9. Off-Site Sales Both the seller and Amazon benefit from promoting products off-site as it not only brings in new-to-brand sales but also creates brand awareness. Page views and sales can be increased by including links on external websites, blog posts, social media etc. 10. Reviews Amazon is all about customer satisfaction and therefore product reviews are one of the decisive ranking factors. A high number of reviews will rank a product higher in search results than those with few or no reviews. Want a free audit and actionable steps on how to improve your PPC? SCAN THIS! documents.name: A guide to AMAZON PPC Campaign Setup.pdf
documents.content: A G U I D E TO A M A ZO N P P C Campaign Setup A successful Amazon marketing strategy starts with a PPC campaign blueprint. Optimal ad performance is achieved by having well planned, consistent campaign structures and nomenclature and if set up correctly, allows you to execute a more precise approach to optimization and reporting. GOALS OF AN AMAZON PPC STRATEGY Generate Sales Increase ad discovery and visibility boosts sales Improve Organic Rank Driving sales velocity with relevant, top of search keywords Generate Data Discovery of new profitable search terms for launching campaigns and listing optimization The Amazon advertising console is arranged according to hierarchical levels. Having a consistent and systematic approach to structuring and naming these levels facilitates effective optimization to save you time and ultimately save on wasted ad spend. Portfolio 1 Parent Product Campaign 1 Ad Group Ad Group Max 5 keywords PORTFOLIOS As well as being an effective organizational tool, portfolios are a valuable way to effectively monitor and report product performance. As each parent product is promoted by multiple campaigns, keeping one portfolio per parent product makes workflow easier to manage and provides valuable insight and control over campaigns CAMPAIGNS Separating both auto and manual campaigns based on match type outputs a higher grade of data and provides better control over campaign performance. With campaign budget distribution up to Amazon’s discretion, we see that those campaigns containing more than one match type have an uneven distribution of budget with some match types receiving more of the budget than others. Additionally, by separating each match type you are able to monitor and scale more effectively at both the budget and the bid level, as well as simplifying data monitoring and analysis. AD GROUPS Limiting each campaign to only one ad group allows you to improve both scaling and optimization efficiency as 100% of the budget is focused solely on that ad group. Confining campaigns to one ad group and one match type is the best solution for gaining control over budget distribution and scaling for profitability. NOTE: test with all campaign and match types to harvest new profitable keywords and increase sales volume KEYWORDS Unequal distribution of sessions and spend can occur when ad groups are subject to keyword dumping as the number of keywords within an ad group dramatically impacts the performance of the campaign. Campaigns achieve optimal output when keywords/product targets are limited to a maximum of 5 per ad group. For example, an ad group with 15- 20 keywords results in the top 5 generating 80-100% of the sales. Also, segregating high search volume and low search volume keywords will see that each keyword gets the opportunity to perform. When keywords of varying search volume are grouped together, the spend goes to the higher converting keyword, leaving keywords that could convert, with low or no impressions. Below is a summary outlining our most successful strategy for Amazon Sponsored Product Advertising. documents.name: 5 top strategies for winning amazon product launch.pdf
documents.content: 5 T O P S T R AT E G I E S F O R A W I N N I N G A M A Z O N P R O D U C T L A U N C H BY: MINA ELIAS, TRIVIUM Have you ever wondered how some products on Amazon seem to take off while others struggle to gain traction? On the world’s largest ecommerce platform, where millions of sellers vie for consumers’ attention, having a great product just isn’t enough. Achieving success is about launching products to capture — and retain — customers’ interest. A successful Amazon product launch can make or break your business. To ensure a winning product launch, you need a well-planned strategy that includes research, marketing, and optimization. Here are five key product launch strategies that not only meet the needs of your target market, but also generate revenue and growth for your business. 1. Learn About Your Market A surefire way to create a lackluster launch? Not conducting marketing research. Without knowing how to meet customer needs or stand out in a crowded marketplace, businesses can launch products that result in low sales, negative reviews, or even a damaged reputation that can be difficult to recover from. By conducting thorough market research, identifying market gaps, and pinpointing potential demand before launching a product, on the other hand, you can ensure that your product fills a specific need. Analyzing fundamental aspects, such as market demand, profitability, suppliers, delivery, and target audience, plays a crucial role in validating the potential success of a product. Amazon provides several tools for market research, including the Best Sellers listings, the Movers and Shakers list, and the ability to browse Amazon storefronts. Tools like ManageByStats and D8aDriven can also help you find profitable products by analyzing metrics such as sales volume, keyword search volume, and pricing. By utilizing these tools, you can identify products with high demand and low competition and track your competitors' sales trends, pricing strategies, and marketing tactics. 2. Conduct Keyword Research Keyword research is an essential aspect of any new Amazon product launch strategy. The process enables you to identify the most relevant keywords and phrases that potential customers use when searching for products similar to yours. After you’ve found the right keywords, incorporating them into your pay-per-click (PPC) ad campaigns to improve your search ranking and increase your visibility to customers is easy with management software like PPC Entourage. The result: a big revenue boost. Amazon provides a wealth of information that sellers can use for keyword research, such as the search bar autocomplete feature and the suggested search terms that appear at the bottom of the search results page. Analyzing your competitors’ listings can also give you valuable insights into the keywords they’re targeting and the language they’re using to describe their products. You can also use third-party tools to identify keywords relevant to your products and gain insights into each keyword’s search volume and competition level. By using a combination of Amazon, competitor listings, and third-party tools, you can create a comprehensive list of targeted keywords that will help you optimize your product listings, give you maximum visibility into your products’ performance, and increase your chances of success on Amazon. 3. Optimize Your Product Listing Keywords are essential, but if they’re not connected to a compelling product listing, an Amazon product launch can fall flat. As you craft your product listing, ensure you incorporate SEO elements, engaging A+ content, and a captivating brand story. When you leverage quality research and insights into products and your competitors with SellerTools, you can make sure you’re maximizing your listing. By optimizing the product listing with relevant keywords and providing valuable information about your brand, you can enhance the visibility of your products and establish a strong online presence. Here are a few areas to pay attention to. PRODUCT IMAGES Today’s consumers expect an enhanced experience when they visit your product pages. Incorporating high-quality images and videos that showcase your product's use, features, and benefits is crucial for creating an exceptional customer experience and boosting conversion rates. By providing visual aids, you can present information in a more engaging and interactive way, allowing customers to quickly discover your product’s unique benefits and features. TITLE AND BULLET POINTS Two must-have features of your Amazon product listing: a compelling title and bullet points. Your product title should be clear, concise, and attention-grabbing. A well-crafted title accurately reflects the product and includes relevant keywords that enable customers to quickly find it in search. Bullet points should highlight the product's key features and benefits, making it easy for customers to understand what they're getting. They should be short, straightforward, and easy to read and understand. Similarly to the title, including relevant keywords in the bullet points can improve the product's visibility and help it rank higher in search results. BRAND STORY, PRODUCT DESCRIPTIONS, AND A+ CONTENT Your brand story is your opportunity to connect with potential customers on a deeper level and differentiate your product from competitors. This section should be authentic and compelling, providing insight into your brand's values, mission, and history. Use storytelling techniques to engage potential customers and create an emotional connection. A strong brand story can increase brand loyalty and create brand advocates who will spread the word about your product. The product description should be clear, concise, and engaging, providing potential customers with all the information they need to make an informed purchasing decision. Use bullet points and short paragraphs to craft an accessible description, and incorporate relevant keywords to increase search visibility. Most importantly, ensure that the product description accurately reflects the product and explains how the product can benefit a user. A+ content is an additional opportunity to showcase your product's key features and benefits by using enhanced images, videos, and additional text to provide a more immersive customer experience. Because A+ content offers a more comprehensive view of the product, it can improve conversion rates and increase customer satisfaction. documents.name: UNDERSTANDING THE AMAZON SHOPPER.pdf
documents.content: U N D E R S TA N D I N G T H E A M A Z O N S H O P P E R Amazon consistently maintains the majority share of the online retail market. Understanding consumer buying behavior can be a valuable asset to ensure your success on the platform. Interestingly, Amazon shoppers have, unknowingly, been “coached” to browse and buy on the Amazon interface. Purchase decisions have been made easy as buyers are tuned into what they are seeing and what features they are looking for when choosing a product on Amazon. UNDERSTANDING AUDIENCES AND BUYER BEHAVIOUR ON AMAZON Surveys analyzing Amazon buyer behaviour show the biggest factors buyers consider when making a purchase include: Price – 41.1% No of ratings and reviews – 16.2% Convincing product descriptions/photos – 7.7% Convenience of shopping (Prime membership) – 22.7% Prior experience with the product/brand – 9.1% So to cater your business strategy to “win” shoppers on Amazon, it is important to understand that there are 3 stages of product disqualification. · Stage 1 · Stage 2 · Stage 3 Product ad appears The shopper The shopper opens up in the search- and if reviews the product a competitor product desirable is click detail page and if page, a determines if on, if undesirable, optimized, they do they disqualifies them it is disqualified. not disqualify you. and return to product page for a conversion. STAGE 1 Product Listing – Win the Search Amazon search result pages are a buyer's first insight into the available products. It is also where they make their initial disqualifications of product listings which do not appeal to them. In this situation, first impressions are key to winning a buyer over your competitors. To be compelling and attract buyer attention, it is vital to address and optimize each element of a product ad. 7 1 2 3 5 6 4 1. Main Image High quality photography The image fills the square Transparent background Text on the label and packaging is clear and easy to read No additional text outside of the product 2. Product Title Clear and concise and with a text flow that explains the product and that a buyer can understand. Importantly, it must include the keywords that buyers are searching for. 3. Star Rating and Review Count The higher the star reviews and the higher the rating count, the more likely a buyer will choose a product ad over others, amazon shoppers really care about reviews. 4. Shipping Speed Shoppers desire fast shipping options. Unless you can compete with Prime’s 1–2-day shipping option, FBA will always outperform FBM. 5. Price Pricing is a major factor influencing product disqualification. While offering the lowest price is not essential, remaining competitive, with a validated offer, is key to winning a click over your competitors. Buyers will spend the time determining which product is more economical and which product is better value for money. 6. Coupons Coupons differentiate one ad from another and capture the attention of buyers. If buyer 's decision is tight, they will most often opt for the product offering a coupon. 7. Seller Badges BestSeller and Amazon’s choice badges create consumer confidence. Not only does the badge placement on a product ad draw attention but sellers awarded with badges see significantly improved sales. STAGE 2 Product Listing – Win the Search At this point you have passed stage 1. You have “won” the product ad selection over your competitors. Stage 2 is about converting a sale. The details of a product page are responsible for convincing a buyer not only to make a purchase, but that they in fact have a need and a desire for your product. The elements of a product page that should be optimized are: A. Secondary Image Visually explain the features and benefits of your product and highlight why your product is better than your competitors. B. Rest of Images Images should be both visual and information based, featuring the benefits and aimed at providing the solution to which the customer is seeking. With 70% of shoppers dropping off after the second image, it is crucial that every image provides a reason for purchase. C. Bullet Points Serve 2 purposes; convincing a buyer to make a purchase as well as keyword ranking. More often than not, shoppers will not read the entire bullet point but rather scan over any highlighted keywords. It is important to capitalize the main selling points or benefits of the product. The remainder of the text should be heavily focused on relevant keywords for improved product ranking. D. Products Related to This Item Competitors ads targeting your product can divert traffic away from your product page. Launching campaigns targeting your own products will utilize this space and reduce the space occupied by competing products. E. A+ Content Content that is text heavy reduces conversion rates. Buyers may disqualify a product if they are overwhelmed with text and if it is too time consuming to explore the features and benefits of a product. Opting for image rich descriptions and clearly outlining selling points allows you to showcase your brand. F. Videos for This Product Videos weigh heavily on buyer influence and disqualification. Offering a live visual of your product helps shoppers convert effectively. Utilizing influencers for comparison and unboxing videos are a powerful means of influencing a sale and retaining a shopper on your product page. G. Customer Questions and Answers By building a FAQ you are effectively eliminating purchase doubt in a shopper’s mind. The number of questions received and answered, not only indicates social proof but creates legitimacy of the product and the brand. H. Reviews Provide very strong social proof and brand trust with shoppers on Amazon. Product rating is high on the list of buyer intent and most shoppers will disqualify any product with a below 4-star rating. I. Visit the Store Located under the title, before buyers disqualify a product, they will often base their opinion on how a brand is presented in a store. A store should be professionally established with an attractive landing page to create buyer trust. STAGE 3 Competitor Product Page Having ticked the boxes at stage 1 and stage 2, potential customers now have the possibility of making a purchase at the front of their mind. The final hurdle is disqualification of your competitors. Buyer behaviour will see that the majority of shoppers will explore at least one competitor before making their final decision. This is where it is key that you have addressed and optimized all the elements at stage 1 and stage 2 to ensure you entice the buyer back to your listing for a conversion. IN CONCLUSION With more people opting for online shopping than ever before, paying close attention to the key factors that influence buyer behavior and drive consumers to make a purchase and addressing these factors is essential for any business to succeed. documents.name: AN AMAZON  ADVERTISING STRATEGY TO PREPARE FOR Q4.pdf
documents.content: A N A M A Z O N A D V E R T I S I N G S T R AT E G Y T O P R E PA R E F O R Q 4 Create a Solid PPC Strategy Ahead of Time In the annual cycle of an Amazon seller, Q4 can be the most lucrative time of the year. With the Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales, backed up by the busy Christmas shopping period and closely followed by the new year splurges, shoppers are out in full force with their wallets ready. With increased competition and more sellers willing to increase their ad spend during the peak season, it is vital to have a solid PPC strategy in play ahead of the holiday season. When planning a strategy, look at your metrics and define your objectives. Determine where you want to improve and what changes you need to implement in order to meet those objectives. Benchmarking data history, prior to implementing changes, will allow you to monitor your progression. A 3 Step Approach for Sales and Profitability in Q4 As the holiday season approaches, ad costs start to significantly increase at the end of Q3 and do not return to normal until after the new year period. To effectively balance out the higher CPC with the increased sales volume, ranking organically is more beneficial than ever to remain profitable during the peak period. Entering Q4 with a high organic rank, for your top performing keywords, will see you come out the other side with an increase in revenue and more importantly, profitability. STEP 1: Aggressively Scale Campaign Budget & Bids to improve Organic Rank Bidding aggressively will allow you to improve your organic rank and drive free traffic, when the holiday season begins. 45 days prior to the launch of Black Friday, set a high campaign budget and bid aggressively on your top performing keywords. Pay close attention to your sessions. If your tactics are working you should see an increase in sessions, closely related to your increase in ad spend. Be prepared to not be profitable during the lead up to Q4. · High Campaign Budget · High Bid · Boost Organic Rank STEP 2: Test Top of Search Placement With an increase in buyers and sessions, comes an increase in window shoppers. Particularly in the week leading up to Black Friday. To avoid attracting window shoppers at the top of search, optimize your ad placement well in advance. Test with bid by placement to determine if your product is a top of search purchase or if it performs best in product pages or rest of search. Knowing where your customers are purchasing will allow you to determine the optimal placement for your product ad. · Top of Search First Page? · Product Pages? · Rest of Search? STEP 3: Scale for Profitability Entering Q4 With Black Friday being the opening event to Q4, use it as a benchmark to start scaling back the high budget and keyword bids. Having achieved a high organic rank for relevant keywords, reducing the bids 1 week prior to Black Friday will see you well positioned to enter the holiday season. A high, organic position in the search results will drive increased sales without relying on the high PPC typically seen during the peak season. · Decrease Campaign Budget · Decrease Bids · Monitor Organic Rank Conclusion Q4 is the opportune time for sellers on Amazon to increase revenue. By creating and executing a solid, detailed PPC plan of attack ahead of time will see the required results achieved. Follow your plan and be prepared for the most intense shopping time of the year! documents.name: optimising amazon campaigns with negative keywords.pdf
documents.content: O P T I M I Z I N G A M A Z O N C A M PA I G N S W I T H N E G AT I V E K E Y W O R D S Adding negative keywords is one of the most important and one of the biggest impacting campaign optimizations that you should regularly perform. While it might seem counterintuitive, taking the time to identify search terms that are irrelevant or have clicks and no sales can actually result in higher conversion rates and better returns on your ad spend. What are Negative Keywords? Negative keywords are the search terms, used by customers, that you don't want your Amazon Ads to appear for. They are the exact opposite of your target keywords, and their main purpose is to prevent your ads from showing up for irrelevant or inappropriate searches. Using negative keywords, you can save on your advertising budget and improve the relevance and performance of your ads. How do you Optimize Negative Keywords? Optimizing your negative keywords is a crucial step to ensure that your Amazon Ads are displayed only for the relevant searches. Your search terms report will show you the actual search terms that triggered your ads. By analyzing this report, you can identify the irrelevant or non-profitable searches and add them as negative keywords. · Search terms with high clicks and no sales · Search terms with high spend and no sales · Irrelevant search terms Phrase match negative keywords will exclude your ads from searches that contain the exact phrase, while exact match negative keywords will exclude your ads from searches that match the exact keyword. This can help you to exclude specific searches that are not relevant to your product. How will it Improve Performance? Using negative keywords can improve the performance of your Amazon Ads in several ways: 1. Save on your advertising budget: By excluding irrelevant searches, you can prevent your ads from being displayed to users who are not interested in your product. This can help you to save your advertising budget and invest it in more relevant searches. 2. Improve your click-through rate (CTR): By displaying your ads only for relevant searches, you can improve your CTR. This is because users who are interested in your product are more likely to click on your ad and visit your product page. 3. Improve your conversion rate: By displaying your ads only for relevant searches, you can also improve your conversion rate. This is because users who are interested in your product are more likely to make a purchase or take the desired action on your product page. In conclusion, using negative keywords is an essential step in optimizing your Amazon Ads. By analyzing your search terms report and adding relevant negative keywords, you can improve the performance of your ads, save your advertising budget, and reach your target audience more effectively. They are the exact opposite of your target keywords, and their main purpose is to prevent your ads from showing up for irrelevant or inappropriate searches. Using negative keywords, you can save on your advertising budget and improve the relevance and performance of your ads. How do you Optimize Negative Keywords? Optimizing your negative keywords is a crucial step to ensure that your Amazon Ads are displayed only for the relevant searches. Your search terms report will show you the actual search terms that triggered your ads. By analyzing this report, you can identify the irrelevant or non-profitable searches and add them as negative keywords. · Search terms with high clicks and no sales · Search terms with high spend and no sales · Irrelevant search terms Phrase match negative keywords will exclude your ads from searches that contain the exact phrase, while exact match negative keywords will exclude your ads from searches that match the exact keyword. This can help you to exclude specific searches that are not relevant to your product. How will it Improve Performance? Using negative keywords can improve the performance of your Amazon Ads in several ways: 1. Save on your advertising budget: By excluding irrelevant searches, you can prevent your ads from being displayed to users who are not interested in your product. This can help you to save your advertising budget and invest it in more relevant searches. 2. Improve your click-through rate (CTR): By displaying your ads only for relevant searches, you can improve your CTR. This is because users who are interested in your product are more likely to click on your ad and visit your product page. 3. Improve your conversion rate: By displaying your ads only for relevant searches, you can also improve your conversion rate. This is because users who are interested in your product are more likely to make a purchase or take the desired action on your product page. In conclusion, using negative keywords is an essential step in optimizing your Amazon Ads. By analyzing your search terms report and adding relevant negative keywords, you can improve the performance of your ads, save your advertising budget, and reach your target audience more effectively. documents.content: 1 0 W A Y S T O B E AT T H E A M A Z O N A L G O R I T H M Amazon works with its own proprietary search algorithm to determine which products are placed at the top of search results and will always promote the products that are most likely to convert. 1. Seller Authority With the aim of providing a positive customer experience, the Amazon algorithm places importance on a seller's previous, as well as current, activity on the platform. Active Time Feedback Performance on Amazon Rating Metrics Inventory Fulfillment Size of Product Levels Method Catalogue 2. Sales History A history of consistent sales, plus sales velocity, weighs heavily on organic rank. The more sales being generated and the higher the potential for sales in the future, the higher Amazon will rank a product. 3. Impressions The more views a product receives, not only on the Amazon Marketplace, but also affiliate and partner sites, the higher Amazon will rank a product. 4. Click-Through-Rate (CTR) CTR represents both ad relevance and customer engagement. A high CTR indicates a high volume of traffic which is indexed by the algorithm to improve product rank. 5. Conversion Rate (CVR) As a measure of the rate at which potential customers view and then buy a product, CVR is a pivotal factor in a better product ranking. A higher conversion rate means more sales which contributes to a higher rank by Amazon’s algorithm. 6. Organic Sales Sales generated from organic product listings, have a powerful influence on the Amazon algorithm. Sales velocity from organic sales is prioritized over sales from paid advertising when it comes to product ranking. 7. PPC Sales PPC is a key driver for increased traffic, CTR, CVR and sales velocity. All of which are important ranking factors and contribute to a solid organic presence. 8. Internal Sales Sales generated from placements other than through search results, such as ‘frequently bought together’, ‘recommended’ or ‘similar products’ will influence product ranking. 9. Off-Site Sales Both the seller and Amazon benefit from promoting products off-site as it not only brings in new-to-brand sales but also creates brand awareness. Page views and sales can be increased by including links on external websites, blog posts, social media etc. 10. Reviews Amazon is all about customer satisfaction and therefore product reviews are one of the decisive ranking factors. A high number of reviews will rank a product higher in search results than those with few or no reviews. Want a free audit and actionable steps on how to improve your PPC? SCAN THIS! documents.content: P P C A N A LY T I C S : T R A C K T H E M O S T I M P O R T A N T M E T R I C S Optimal PPC performance on Amazon requires frequent and consistent optimization. Sellers who actively and efficiently optimize their ad campaigns almost always see better results. To effectively optimize campaign performance, it is essential to have a robust system in place with a manageable workflow procedure. The most critical part of any system is having a clear and concise overview of account performance and a method of tracking performance following optimizations and modifications. Building an analytics dashboard simplifies the process by providing a snapshot of account performance and a 360o view into tracking changes and analyzing how modifications have impacted account metrics. No matter which system you use, there are important consistencies: Have clear objectives Analyze the data Optimize based on the data Review Building an Analytics Dashboard Building an analytics dashboard, in which you enter daily data values, once a week, is an effective way to monitor the performance, from week to week. Using a spreadsheet, such as the one above, will enable identification of percentile changes to key metrics due to campaign and listing optimizations. METRICS TO COLLATE: PPC Spend – paid advertising costs extracted from campaign manager PPC Sales – sales from paid traffic extracted from campaign manager Total Sales – total of organic and sponsored ad sales, extracted from business reports Units – total units sold, both organic and paid, extracted from business reports Sessions – total of organic and paid sessions, extracted from business reports Click through rate (CTR) – the ratio of clicks to impressions, extracted from campaign manager Cost per Click (CPC) – the average cost per click, extracted from campaign manager Sale Price - listing price per unit Amazon Fees – referral and fulfillment fees, extracted from seller central, manage inventory Cost of Goods (COG) – landing cost per unit CALCULATIONS: Units X 100 = Unit Session % Sessions PPC Spend = Cost per session Nº of sessions PPC Spend X 100 = TACoS Total Sales Sale Price - COG - Amazon Fees = Profit PPC Spend Blended = Cost per Acquisition Units What are the main metrics we need to track? When determining which metrics to track, it is important to look at the two key goals of Amazon PPC: 1- To drive traffic for the minimum cost possible · Sessions – are we driving traffic? · Cost per session – at what cost are we driving traffic? · Cost per acquisition – what is the cost to drive traffic for 1 conversion 2- Improve organic rank for long-term sales with no advertising costs · Profit – are we seeing an increase in profit, and units sold, while maintaining a consistent PPC spend? Analyzing the numbers in the dashboard SESSIONS and COST PER SESSION With the first goal in mind, the most important metric to monitor traffic volume is sessions, and when aiming for increased sessions it is important to monitor the cost per session. (Not to be confused, sessions are the number of unique visitors to a listing whereas clicks are the total number of times an ad was clicked). When aiming to increase revenue, such as during keyword discovery, your goal is to increase sessions, which will proportionally produce an increase in spend. Monitoring sessions can assess the effectiveness of the increase in spend. While the ratio will vary, if the aim is to increase spend by 100%, you expect to produce as least a 50-60% growth in sessions. If this is not the case: a) There may be a CTR issue b) Multiple ad types may be being clicked by same buyer – multiple clicks, more spend, but the same number of sessions COST PER ACQUISITION The aggregate cost to acquire one conversion is the cost per sale, or the cost per acquisition (CPA). Changes in CPA reflects the effectiveness of campaign optimizations and it is directly influenced by the cost per session and/or the conversion rate (CVR). A decreased cost per session and an increased conversion rate will reflect an improved CPA. If cost per session remains consistent but the CPA continues to increase, you can determine there is an issue with CVR and vice versa. If you have effectively optimized and lowered the cost per session or have optimized for an increased CVR you will see an improved CPA. Capturing these metrics allows calculated decisions to determine where optimizations should be targeted to lower the cost per acquisition, as lowering the cost for one conversion is proportional to an increase in net profit. PROFIT Your bottom line is the ultimate reference of campaign performance. Viewing a snapshot of profit provides a summary of how optimizations have affected overall account performance. Steps to get Metrics Back on Track 1- To lower the cost per session · Reduce bids on high ACoS keywords · Reduce bids on keywords with clicks and no sales · Adjust bid by placement for low ROAS campaigns · Negative exact non-profitable search terms in auto, broad and phrase campaigns · Pause non-profitable sponsored brand and sponsored display ads · Improve organic rank 2- To lower the cost per acquisition · Lower the cost per session · Optimize the product listing to improve the CVR Want a free audit Assessing the performance of your account and actionable and your optimizations depends on what steps on how to improve your PPC? you are trying to achieve. If you are in a SCAN THIS! discovery phase you are expecting higher spend, increased sessions and lower profits. If in a maintenance phase your goal is to maintain or reduce spend while continuing to drive more profitable traffic and sales.

documents.content: A N A M A Z O N A D V E R T I S I N G S T R AT E G Y T O P R E PA R E F O R Q 4 Create a Solid PPC Strategy Ahead of Time In the annual cycle of an Amazon seller, Q4 can be the most lucrative time of the year. With the Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales, backed up by the busy Christmas shopping period and closely followed by the new year splurges, shoppers are out in full force with their wallets ready. With increased competition and more sellers willing to increase their ad spend during the peak season, it is vital to have a solid PPC strategy in play ahead of the holiday season. When planning a strategy, look at your metrics and define your objectives. Determine where you want to improve and what changes you need to implement in order to meet those objectives. Benchmarking data history, prior to implementing changes, will allow you to monitor your progression. A 3 Step Approach for Sales and Profitability in Q4 As the holiday season approaches, ad costs start to significantly increase at the end of Q3 and do not return to normal until after the new year period. To effectively balance out the higher CPC with the increased sales volume, ranking organically is more beneficial than ever to remain profitable during the peak period. Entering Q4 with a high organic rank, for your top performing keywords, will see you come out the other side with an increase in revenue and more importantly, profitability. STEP 1: Aggressively Scale Campaign Budget & Bids to improve Organic Rank Bidding aggressively will allow you to improve your organic rank and drive free traffic, when the holiday season begins. 45 days prior to the launch of Black Friday, set a high campaign budget and bid aggressively on your top performing keywords. Pay close attention to your sessions. If your tactics are working you should see an increase in sessions, closely related to your increase in ad spend. Be prepared to not be profitable during the lead up to Q4. · High Campaign Budget · High Bid · Boost Organic Rank STEP 2: Test Top of Search Placement With an increase in buyers and sessions, comes an increase in window shoppers. Particularly in the week leading up to Black Friday. To avoid attracting window shoppers at the top of search, optimize your ad placement well in advance. Test with bid by placement to determine if your product is a top of search purchase or if it performs best in product pages or rest of search. Knowing where your customers are purchasing will allow you to determine the optimal placement for your product ad. · Top of Search First Page? · Product Pages? · Rest of Search? STEP 3: Scale for Profitability Entering Q4 With Black Friday being the opening event to Q4, use it as a benchmark to start scaling back the high budget and keyword bids. Having achieved a high organic rank for relevant keywords, reducing the bids 1 week prior to Black Friday will see you well positioned to enter the holiday season. A high, organic position in the search results will drive increased sales without relying on the high PPC typically seen during the peak season. · Decrease Campaign Budget · Decrease Bids · Monitor Organic Rank Conclusion Q4 is the opportune time for sellers on Amazon to increase revenue. By creating and executing a solid, detailed PPC plan of attack ahead of time will see the required results achieved. Follow your plan and be prepared for the most intense shopping time of the year! documents.content: Assignment Questions SECTION 1 1.Explain what is PPC and how it works?(2 marks)2 What is PPC? PPC stands for Pay Per Click and represents a key feature for each business that is selling on Amazon. How does it work? When a user searches for a product on Amazon, they are presented with search results pages and these pages contain both organic and sponsored listings. Sponsored listings are ads placed by Amazon sellers using the Amazon PPC program. When you decide to place a bid for a specific keyword relevant to your product, you compete with other sellers who are bidding on the same keyword. In this case, the seller with the highest bid shows up in a higher position. The goal of PPC is to identify what strategy works best for you and drive quality traffic to your product listing which eventually ends up in conversions. 2.What are the two main goals of PPC? (2 marks)1.5 1. Increase visibility and discoverability. The first goal is to increase the visibility and discoverability of your products on Amazon. This means getting your products in front of more potential customers who are searching for products like yours on the Amazon platform. 2. Drive sales and conversions. Why do we separate auto targeting types into separate campaigns? This section shows the ads that are being displayed on your product detail page. 12. What are brand protection campaigns? Why do we use them? (2 marks) 2 It involves bidding on keywords related to a brand and its products, therefore the brand's own products appear at the top of search results.
